## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

discovered-from:AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.
data.title: Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks

# Dev-mode write-back: gym "Save to repo" persists bot tuning to src/data/bot-tuning.json

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature

**discovered-from:** AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3 (its scope-creep note flagged this path out of scope there)

## Problem statement

Today the Bot Tuning gym persists only to `localStorage` (`ai-hell-bot-tuning`), and the Git-tracked shipped baseline `src/data/bot-tuning.json` must be refreshed manually via the gym **Export** button → overwrite file → commit (documented in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12 and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`). Player ship and enemy/difficulty configs already have a dev-mode write-back path: the Vite CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, served `/api/csv/...` PUT endpoints) writes gym Save/Save-As edits straight into the committed CSVs (`src/core/configStore.ts` `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`). This item gives bot tuning the same convenience: a dev-mode (Vite-serve-only) write path that persists the currently-selected tuning configuration to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`, so a designer does not have to Export → overwrite → commit manually.

## Users

- Designer tuning the demo bot in the Bot Tuning gym — wants a Save action that writes current tuning back to the committed baseline (dev server only).
- Maintainer / release reviewer — wants the write path dev-only and explicit, so a production/static build can never mutate the committed baseline.

Example user stories:

- *As a designer tuning the demo bot, I want a Save action in the Bot Tuning gym to write my current tuning back to `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (dev server only), so the shipped baseline stays in sync without the manual Export → overwrite → commit dance.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the write path to be dev-only and explicit, so a production/static build can never mutate the committed baseline or surprise a distributed user.*

## Desired change

1. **Write endpoint** — expose a dev-only endpoint (e.g. `PUT /api/bot-tuning/`) in the Vite dev-server plugin chain, mirroring the `configCsvPlugin` pattern (allowed-path allowlist, atomic write = temp file + rename, `apply: 'serve'` only). The endpoint validates the incoming blob's shape before writing (reuse the store's `parseState`-style validation / `coerceTuningValues`) and writes the exact `serialiseBotTuningState()` JSON blob to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`.
2. **Gym affordance** — add a "Save to repo" (dev-only) button in the Bot Tuning gym panel, next to Export, that posts the current store state to the endpoint and reports success/failure (`SaveResult`-shaped, like `saveShipConfig`). Disabled or hidden outside dev (`import.meta.env.DEV`, matching `saveShipConfig`'s `isDev()` gate).
3. **Out-of-scope guard** — no runtime behaviour change and no new write path in production; same guard contract as the CSV store (`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` outside dev). Atomic replace must preserve the trailing-newline/pretty-print format the `bot-tuning.json` tests expect (`src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` asserts byte-identity with the store Export plus trailing newline).
4. **Tests** — unit tests for the write helper (valid blob replaces file; invalid blob rejected without touching the file; non-dev returns unavailable; byte round-trip with `serialiseBotTuningState()`), gym-level test that "Save to repo" calls the write path and reflects a real file write, and a plugin-endpoint test mirroring `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` scope. `npm run typecheck` and the full suite stay green; the gym↔game duplicate-body parity guard stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Dev-only write endpoint persists the baseline.** In dev mode, a write of the current `serialiseBotTuningState()` blob updates `src/data/bot-tuning.json` atomically; the file stays byte-identical to the store Export (pretty-print + trailing newline), so `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` round-trip tests pass after the write.
- **AC2 — Invalid input never corrupts the file.** A write with an invalid/unschematised blob fails with a clear `SaveResult` reason and leaves the committed file untouched.
- **AC3 — Production/static builds cannot write.** The endpoint is dev-serve-only and the client gate (`isDev()`) means a production build reports `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` (no mutation of the shipped baseline).
- **AC4 — Gym affordance.** The Bot Tuning gym exposes a dev-only "Save to repo" control that persists the current selection and reports success/failure; hidden/disabled outside dev.
- **AC5 — Tests + validation.** Unit + gym + plugin-endpoint tests cover persistence, rejection, round-trip, and non-dev unavailability; `npm run typecheck`, the full suite, and the parity guard pass.

## Constraints

- No change to bot decision/permission semantics — only a dev-tool persistence path (same scope boundary recorded in AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3).
- Follows the CSV plugin precedent exactly (atomic write, allowed-path allowlist, `apply: serve` only); do not invent a new infra pattern.
- The stored file must stay Git-committable and byte-stable (test contract).
- Out of scope: automatic background sync on every slider move (that would spam writes); the affordance must be an explicit Save action.
- Out of scope: any write path in production/static builds; dev-only via Vite serve.

## Existing state

- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` already exports `serialiseBotTuningState()` (the exact Export blob) and has `parseState`-style (private) schema validation + `coerceTuningValues` from `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`.
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` is the Git-tracked baseline whose byte-format contract is pinned by `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` (pretty-print + trailing newline, byte-identical to fresh-profile Export).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` is the established dev-write infra: `apply: 'serve'`, `/api/csv/...` GET/PUT, atomic write helper, allowed-path allowlist; registered in `vite.config.ts`.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` defines the `SaveResult` / `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` / `isDev()` contract the bot-tuning write should mirror.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` already has the Export button/status readout in `_buildActionRow()` and the panel-status helpers; a "Save to repo" button slots in alongside.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the CSV dev-write pattern to parallel/clone for bot tuning
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — the plugin-endpoint test harness to mirror
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — `serialiseBotTuningState()`, `parseState`/`coerceTuningValues` validation, `BOT_TUNING_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — `coerceTuningValues` / tuning-field schema shared by the store and the write validator
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig` + `SaveResult`/`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` contract to mirror
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — the committed baseline the dev write targets
- `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` — file round-trip/trailing-newline contract the writer must preserve
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — new "Save to repo" control next to Export
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.test.ts` — gym-level write-path test
- `vite.config.ts` — plugin registration
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — update the refresh workflow (dev write vs Export)

## Related work

- `Distributed versions of the game do not use the correct Bot definitions (AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3)` — completed; introduced the bundled baseline this write-back refreshes; its scope-creep note explicitly deferred this dev-mode write path.
- `Gym scene for AI bot tuning (AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0)` — completed; the tuning gym + store.
- `Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL)` — completed; Export/`--bot-config` workflow.
- `Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write (AH-0MUE2MGZM0016U3L)` / `Vite CSV plugin: dev middleware (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation) (AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP)` — completed; the CSV write-back precedent this item parallels.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "Save to repo" writes the full store state** (`serialiseBotTuningState()` blob, all named configs + current selection), i.e. exactly the Export blob. This is the only format the byte-identity test contract accepts (the shipped file is the whole `{ version, current, configs }` state), so the button's "current selection" phrasing means the current exported state. (If instead only the single selected config should be written, the file-format contract would need revisiting — not expected.)
- **Assumption — endpoint shape** follows the CSV-plugin precedent: a dev-only Vite middleware, PUT `/api/bot-tuning/` (or a parallel path under a bot-tuning prefix), validating before atomic write. Exact path is an implementation decision within the pattern.
- **Risk — stale baseline:** unchanged existing risk; the dev write reduces (does not eliminate) manual-drift by making the refresh an explicit action.
- **Risk — surprise writes:** a designer clicking Save expects a repo mutation; mitigations: dev-only gate, explicit button label + tooltip, `SaveResult` feedback.
- **Scope-creep risk:** automatic background sync on every slider move is out of scope (explicit Save only). Record any follow-up ideas as new work items, not scope.

## Verification of existing information

- Verified in repo: `serialiseBotTuningState()` is exported from `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` (byte-identical Export blob); `coerceTuningValues` exported from `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`; `parseStateObject` is private (a small store change or a plugin-local validator may be needed — implementation detail, not a requirement change).
- Verified in repo: `configCsvPlugin` exports `atomicWrite`, uses `apply: 'serve'`, allowed-path allowlist, and its test suite exercises PUT/atomic/validation via a real ephemeral HTTP server with `serve`/`build` modes — the exact harness to mirror.
- Verified in repo: `GymBotTuning._buildActionRow()` already builds Export + status; `GymPlayer._onSave()` shows the `saveShipConfig` status-reporting pattern to mirror.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found (searches: "write-back", "save to repo", "config write"; the closest completed items are the CSV write-back precedent and the scoped-out parent note).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: None required — the seed context (detailed discovered-from description) sufficed to draft a clear brief; the repo confirms the referenced APIs and file-format contract. Assumptions above are flagged for producer confirmation rather than asked, per the intake rule to not ask answerable-by-repo questions.
- Open question (advisory, not blocking): endpoint shape — preferred option **parallel dev-only middleware mirroring `configCsvPlugin`** (explicit path, keeps CSV plugin untouched and its tests stable); alternative is extending the CSV plugin's allowlist (rejected: not a CSV, and would complicate the CSV plugin's schema).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV9LCWVI002TOK7** – Add bundled baseline bot-tuning JSON file (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9** – CSV seed data files (enemy-configs.csv, ship-config.csv) (completed)
- **AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL** – Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv9gzd2c005iiu3, ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+210 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5, action (+192 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+186 more)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28T04:58:50Z — Auto-plan pre-check returned `skip` (effort Small, risk Low); six automated review stages run on existing content.
- Completeness review added `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` (`coerceTuningValues`) to **Key Files**.
- AC coverage review: `proceed` — 5/5 acceptance criteria covered; no child decomposition required for this small item.
- Effort/risk refreshed via effort-and-risk skill: Small / Low (score 1), recommended ~7.67h.

# More Force Field feedback: persistent permanent bubble (dimmed when spent) + intercept flash/SFX

## Problem statement

Two player-facing gaps in the Force Field (Gradius-homage reflector, AH-0MV1BIX1W006XF95):

1. **Bubble** — when the Force Field is **permanent** (hold-full reward), its bubble graphic disappears: it reads as if the temporary pickup timer removed it. This is a bug: `drawForceFieldBubble` (`src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts:304`) gates the draw on `registry.remaining('force_field')` — the **temporary window countdown**. A permanent-only field is stored with `remaining: 0` (`_startOrRefreshTimed`, `src/powerups/effects.ts:687`) and a permanent base whose temp window has expired is reset to `remaining = 0` (`_expireTimedEffect`), so the bubble is drawn for at most the temp window (base 8 s) and then cleared even though `isForceFieldActive()` is still true for the whole run.
2. **Intercept feedback** — when the field reflects a bullet there is no flash and no sound; the interception is easy to miss. `CombatScene._reflectEnemyBullet` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:1528`) only spawns the reflected bullet.

**Producer decisions (recorded in the Appendix, Q1–Q3):** (Q1) a spent field must stay visible but **dimmed**; (Q2) the intercept flash is a bounce-point flash **plus a new baked ToneForge cue**; (Q3) issue type `feature`.

## Users

- As a player who has earned the permanent Force Field, I want the bubble to stay visible for the rest of the run, so I can read that my field is active.
- As a player, when my field can no longer reflect I want it to dim rather than vanish, so I can tell "the field is up but spent" from "the field expired" (and never confuse it with the temp-pickup timer).
- As a player, I want every intercepted bullet to flash at the bounce point and make its own sound, so I can tell "the field bounce" from "I got hit".
- As a maintainer, I want the feedback to live once in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/` + shared helpers) and the baked-cue pipeline, so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` distinguishes **permanent** base effects from **temporary windows** on top (AC1/AC2 of the player force-field work): `_timed` entries carry `permanent`, `tempWindow`, `remaining`. A permanent-only field never counts down (`tick` skips it, `src/powerups/effects.ts:727-728`) and the HUD already renders it as `∞` via `powerUpTemporaryRemaining(id)` (returns `undefined` for a permanent base with no window). `forceFieldRemaining()` returns the live reflect budget (`_forceFieldRemaining`, 0 when exhausted).
- `drawForceFieldBubble` is already shared and called every frame by `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene`; it pulses the rim continuously and brightens the fill in the final second of the countdown (mirroring the Shield bubble, AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC).
- Shared feedback precedents:
  - `spawnBulletImpact` (`src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`) — self-destroying flash with a trackable `registry`; origin AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR; used by the enemy-force-field absorb seam (AH-0MVM8GW7W004SI0E AC3) and per-identity player-hit impacts (`_spawnEnemyBulletHitImpact`, `CombatScene.ts:1511`).
  - Baked-cue pipeline (ToneForge migration AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J): every baked cue gets a data-only recipe in `audio/toneforge/recipes/` (`aihell-*.yaml`), a manifest entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (cue name → recipe, delivery `baked`, reserved seeds), is rendered deterministically by `node scripts/build-audio.mjs [--render]` (local CLI at `/usr/local/bin/tf`) into `public/audio/sfx/<recipe>.<seed>.wav`, and is checksum-pinned in `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`. The audio contract suite (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) asserts every sound-producing cue export is manifest-mapped, and the amplitude-balance guard (`scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` + test) pins per-cue RMS tiers.
- The reflect branch is one shared loop in `CombatScene` (enemy bullets vs player, where `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` succeeds); `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts:3260` pins `_reflectEnemyBullet` as shared, so feedback added there reaches the game and every gym with no scene edits.

## Desired change

1. **Permanent bubble persistence + spent-dim.**
   - Change the draw gate from `registry.remaining('force_field')` to the temporary-window semantics already used by the HUD (AC1/AC2 of AH-0MV1BIX1W006XF95): draw while `isForceFieldActive()` and there is either an active temporary window or a permanent base. Recommended implementation: gate on `powerUpTemporaryRemaining('force_field')` (`undefined` = permanent-only → draw; else the window countdown as today). Alternative: add an explicit `isForceFieldPermanent()` accessor.
   - **Spent-dim (Q1 = b):** while the field is active but its reflect budget is exhausted (`forceFieldRemaining() <= 0`), draw the bubble in a **dimmed** style — new exported constants for reduced stroke/fill alpha (e.g. `FORCE_FIELD_SPENT_STROKE_ALPHA`, `FORCE_FIELD_SPENT_FILL_ALPHA`, distinctly fainter than the active alphas but still visible). A spent bubble reads "up but inert", never "expired". The dim applies to **both** permanent and temporary fields whenever the budget is spent (cohesive rule; derived from Q1 — a temp field whose budget ran out mid-window also dims).
   - **Expiry cue preserved:** the existing final-second ending brighten continues to apply to a *temporary* window relative to its current baseline (active or spent-dim), so a temp field's wind-down stays readable on top of the dim baseline. A permanent-only field has no ending brighten (no countdown).
2. **Intercept flash (bounce-point) + new baked cue (Q2 = c).**
   - In the shared reflect branch, on every successful `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()`, spawn a short-lived flash at the intercept point via the shared impact seam (`spawnBulletImpact(this, x, y, { registry: this.bulletImpactEffects, color: FORCE_FIELD_COLOR })`).
   - Add a **new dedicated baked cue** `playForceFieldReflectSound()`:
     - New data-only ToneForge recipe `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-forcefield-reflect.yaml` — a short bright "bounce" distinct from both the bullet-destruction tick and the enemy-field break cue; amplitude tier: subtle one-shot, target RMS 0.055 ±1.5 dB (matching `aihell-bullet-destruction`).
     - Manifest entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`: `{ cue: playForceFieldReflectSound, recipe: aihell-forcefield-reflect, delivery: baked, seeds: [32276] }` (next free seed; current used range tops out at 32275).
     - Render with the deterministic pipeline (`node scripts/build-audio.mjs --render`; `tf` CLI is installed) and commit the new `public/audio/sfx/aihell-forcefield-reflect.32276.wav` plus updated `checksums.json`. `audio/toneforge/pin.json` is the toolchain pin — do **not** change it.
     - Export `playForceFieldReflectSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts` → `playCue('playForceFieldReflectSound')`, with the cue decision documented in a comment (in contrast to the *alias* `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound`, which reuses an existing asset — this one is baked fresh per Q2 = c).
   - Audio contract suite picks the cue up from the manifest automatically; the balance guard must stay green (add an amplitude-tier entry for the new cue if the guard's rule requires it).
3. **Parity** — all gameplay changes land in shared modules (`CombatScene`, `CombatEffectVisuals`, `audio/effects.ts`); the three scene call sites require no edits. The cue pipeline is repo-level (`audio/`, `public/`, `scripts/`), unaffected by scenes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Permanent bubble persists:** with a permanent (hold-full) Force Field and no temporary window, `drawForceFieldBubble` returns true (draws) while `isForceFieldActive()` is true, every frame, for the whole run — including after any prior temp window on top of it has expired. Unit test with a permanent-only fake registry in `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`.
- **AC2 — Spent field dims, never vanishes:** while the field is active but the reflect budget is exhausted (`forceFieldRemaining() <= 0`), the bubble is drawn with the reduced spent-state alphas (new exported constants pinned by test), for permanent and temporary fields alike; the bubble is **not** cleared by budget exhaustion. A spent permanent bubble sits steady (no ending brighten); a spent temporary bubble still runs its final-second ending brighten relative to the dim baseline.
- **AC3 — Temporary window behaviour unchanged:** with an active temporary window (with or without a permanent base underneath) and positive reflect budget, the bubble is drawn with the existing final-second brighten; at expiry of a temporary-only field the graphics are cleared (existing tests stay green).
- **AC4 — Expiry still clears:** inactive field → graphics cleared, `drawForceFieldBubble` returns false (existing tests stay green).
- **AC5 — Intercept flash:** every bullet the field reflects spawns one short-lived flash at the intercept point, registered in the shared `bulletImpactEffects` registry (observable in tests), coloured `FORCE_FIELD_COLOR` (0x33ffcc).
- **AC6 — Intercept SFX (new baked cue):** every reflected bullet plays `playForceFieldReflectSound()`; the cue has a manifest entry (recipe `aihell-forcefield-reflect`, delivery `baked`, seed 32276), a rendered WAV committed under `public/audio/sfx/`, an updated `checksums.json`, and a callable export in `src/audio/effects.ts` with the decision documented. The audio contract suite (cue coverage) and the amplitude-balance guard stay green.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity:** flash and cue fire from the shared `CombatScene` reflect branch, so `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene` get them with no scene edits; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard stays green; no new divergent copies.
- **AC8 — Test coverage:** at least one unit test per changed seam: bubble persistence (AC1), spent-dim rendering (AC2), the reflect-feedback seam (flash + cue once per intercept), the manifest/cue-coverage contract, and the shared constants.
- **AC9 — Testing/validation:** the implementation is validated by the repo's test workflow; AC1–AC8 regression tests pass.
- **AC10 — Docs:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — at minimum the `force_field` row in `docs/Game Design Document.md` (permanent bubble persists and dims when spent; reflected bullets flash at the bounce point with a dedicated cue), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (new cue row + seed + amplitude tier), and code comments in the touched modules (CHANGELOG.md excluded — owned by the ship pipeline).
- **AC11 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Shared-core only; no scene-local copies of the feedback (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- No new player-facing UI. One new baked audio asset is explicitly authorised (Q2 = c); `audio/toneforge/pin.json` is unchanged.
- Reflect-budget **semantics** unchanged — the budget still caps reflections at its resolved count with no regeneration; only the visual spent state is added. (The permanent-field budget-regeneration gap is tracked separately in **AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P** — Permanent Force Field should regenerate its reflect budget.)
- Surgical diff: touch the gate + spent-dim constants, the reflect branch, the cue recipe/manifest/export, and docs.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (+ `CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`) — bubble draw gate incl. spent-dim state + constants.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — reflect branch feedback call site (flash + cue).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` (+ `effects.contract.test.ts`) — `playForceFieldReflectSound()` export + cue decision comment; contract coverage.
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-forcefield-reflect.yaml` — **new** data-only recipe.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new baked-cue entry (seed 32276).
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-forcefield-reflect.32276.wav` + `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — rendered asset (via `node scripts/build-audio.mjs --render`).
- `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` (+ test) — amplitude tier for the new cue (verify-only unless required).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — `force_field` power-up row (line ~880).
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — new cue row/seed/tier.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — permanence accessor only if the explicit-accessor alternative is chosen (`powerUpTemporaryRemaining` already exists).
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — reused flash (no change expected).
- Verify-only call sites (no edits expected): `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (~3707), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (~1179), `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` (~468).

## Related work

- `AH-0MV1BIX1W006XF95` (done) — Gradius force field reflector: owns the bubble, reflect budget and permanent/temp semantics the fix builds on.
- `AH-0MVM8GW7W004SI0E` (done) — Shared force-field bubble feedback (enemy side): the absorb/break feedback precedent; also hosts the shared visual module this fix edits.
- `AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR` (done) — When player shoots enemy bullet it should explode: origin of `spawnBulletImpact`.
- `AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC` (done) — Shields need to pulse and fade when ending: the countdown-brighten pattern mirrored in the field bubble.
- `AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J` (done) — Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge: the baked-cue pipeline this work extends.
- `AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51` (done) — Author game-specific ToneForge recipes: recipe authoring conventions (`audio/toneforge/README.md`).
- `AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD` (done) — deterministic WAV build pipeline + checksums.
- `AH-0MVD02WZI004QCTP` (done) — amplitude-tier retune (RMS bands; balance guard).
- `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` (done) — gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md: scope constraint for this item.
- `AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P` (open) — Permanent Force Field should regenerate its reflect budget: the follow-up discovered by the Q1 = b decision (a spent permanent field would otherwise stay dim and inert for the rest of the run).
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (power-ups table), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (cue catalogue).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUADK77K008RBMB** – Provide feedback when changing volume settings (completed) — loose "feedback" keyword match only; not on-point, retained for auditability.
- **AH-0MV822CE7004MQ14** – Arc projectile visuals & feel (completed) — projectile VFX precedent, peripheral.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed) — bullet-theme match only, not on-point.

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: also, bullet, feedback, feels, flash (+13 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: also, bullet, feedback, flash, forcefield (+12 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: also, bullet, feedback, flash, forcefield (+11 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — gate semantics:** `powerUpTemporaryRemaining('force_field')` is `undefined` both for a permanent-only field and when the effect is absent; the gate must check `isForceFieldActive()` first (already the structure of `drawForceFieldBubble`).
- **Risk — baked-cue pipeline:** the new recipe must land inside the amplitude balance band (0.055 RMS subtle one-shot ±1.5 dB) or the guard fails; render determinism is enforced by the pipeline (double-render SHA compare), and `checksums.json` must be committed with the WAV.
- **Assumption — spent-dim applies to temp fields too:** derived from Q1 = b for cohesion; a temp field whose budget runs out mid-window dims as well (recorded in AC2). If the producer intended dimming for permanent only, AC2 narrows.
- **Assumption — expiry cue on top of dim:** the ending brighten for a temporary window is preserved relative to the current baseline (AC2). Alternative (flat dim, no brighten) is a one-line change.
- **Assumption — new cue distinctness for Q2 = c:** the reflect cue is a short bright bounce layered at subtle-one-shot level; if gameplay calls for a louder cue, that is a re-tier of AC6, not a blocker.
- **Assumption — AC baseline:** "the field intercepts a bullet" == a successful `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` (bubble active + budget available), not an exhaust-budget check.
- **Scope creep guard:** permanent-field reflect-budget regeneration (filed as **AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P**), per-hit bubble dimming, and applying a reflect flash to enemy-field absorbs are recorded as follow-ups, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When the Force Field is permanent, once its reflect budget (base 3, cap 10) is spent, should the bubble still be shown?" Options: (a) yes, keep it fully visible; (b) yes, but **dim** it so "spent" reads at a glance; (c) hide it. **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "1. b - dim".** Accepted: **b — dimmed spent state**. Interpretation recorded: dim whenever the field cannot reflect, permanent and temporary alike (AC2). Source: interactive reply (2026-10-25), recorded on AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14.
- Q2: "What should the intercept flash look like, and which SFX cue?" Options: (a) bounce-point flash + reuse the bullet-destruction tick (alias pattern, as the enemy-field break uses); (b) whole-bubble/rim pulse + new baked cue; (c) **bounce-point flash + a new baked ToneForge cue**. **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "2. c".** Accepted: **c — bounce-point flash + new baked cue** (`aihell-forcefield-reflect`, seed 32276, subtle one-shot tier; see AC5/AC6). Source: interactive reply (2026-10-25), recorded on AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14.
- Q3: "Is the missing permanent-bubble behaviour a bug or a feedback feature, and what priority?" **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "3. feature".** Accepted: **issue type `feature`, priority `medium`** (priority unchanged from the original item). Source: interactive reply (2026-10-25), recorded on AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14.

*Research:* read `drawForceFieldBubble` + its tests (`CombatEffectVisuals`) and `_startOrRefreshTimed`/`tick`/`_expireTimedEffect`/`powerUpTemporaryRemaining`/`forceFieldRemaining` (`effects.ts`), the shared reflect branch + `_reflectEnemyBullet` (`CombatScene.ts`), `spawnBulletImpact` (`vfx/bulletImpact.ts`), `thornsAbsorb.ts` and `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound` (`audio/effects.ts`), the ToneForge manifest/recipes/build pipeline and the audio contract + amplitude-balance guard. Root cause for AC1 confirmed: the visual gates on the temp countdown, which is 0 for permanent-only fields. No duplicate/overlapping completed item found.


## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-28 — Plan** (session herdr-1793147056-2932517-28198): decomposed into 3 children (plan/skill): bubble persistence + spent-dim (AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z), intercept feedback with new baked reflect cue (AH-0MVRDMMYO002SC5V), docs + full-suite verification (AH-0MVRDMO9T0068VZQ). All 11 parent ACs covered (tree-coverage 100%, action proceed); six automated review stages run; deps wired (verification blocked by both slices); effort/risk recomputed Small/Medium (E 7.92 h, recommended 9.92 h, risk 9/25). Test-first: TDD is enforced within each item by the implement skill (repo gate forbids committing red tests), so no separate test-only children were created — recorded deviation.

In the descriptions of power ups and weapons on the hull full screen the descriptions should be given two lines

---

## Plan clarifications (plan skill, downtime run)

**Goal (user story):** As a player who fills the mineral hold, I want each power-up/weapon description in the hold-full choice to have room for **two lines** of text, so longer descriptions stay readable and on-screen instead of running past the edge of the 960 x 540 playfield.

**Terminology clarification — "hull full screen".** Read as the **hold-full choice overlay** (`src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, heading `HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP`) — the ship's (cargo) hold filling up. It is the only full-screen surface that renders power-up/weapon descriptions beneath each option; the gym help overlay already word-wraps its descriptions (`src/scenes/HelpScene.ts`), while `MineralChoiceScene` currently renders each description as a **single unwrapped** Phaser text (13 px monospace, no `wordWrap`).

**Current behaviour (evidence).** Row layout is a fixed three-line block: name at `y`, description at `y + 28`, detail (change summary / `★ New`) at `y + 48`, row pitch 84 px (`CHOICE_ROW_PITCH`). The longest power-up description is 210 characters (Teleport) and the longest weapon description 107 characters (Arc); at 13 px monospace an unwrapped line is wider than the 960 px playfield, so long descriptions visibly overflow today.

**Assumption (documented, non-blocking).** "Two lines" means the description **area** must accommodate up to two wrapped lines (layout capacity), not that the shared catalogue copy is rewritten to be exactly two lines. This follows the title's "to allow for more content" and keeps the catalogue copy (and gym-help parity) unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Two-line description area.** Each option's description renders with `wordWrap` constrained to a readable width and `maxLines: 2`, so descriptions up to two lines display fully inside the 960 x 540 playfield.
- **AC2 — No overlap / no regression.** Name -> description (one or two lines) -> change summary / `★ New` remain a non-overlapping vertical block, and consecutive option rows never collide — verified by a scene test that asserts rendered bounds.
- **AC3 — Overflow safety.** A description longer than two lines is truncated to two lines (ellipsis or clipping) and never overflows the playfield horizontally.
- **AC4 — Backward-compatible contracts.** One-line descriptions still render as one line; an option with no description still renders no description line; `getOptionLabels()`, `getDescriptionLines()` and `getDetailLines()` keep their existing contracts.
- **AC5 — Single source of copy.** Descriptions stay resolved from the shared catalogue via `getHelpDescription` (`src/utils/gymHelp.ts`) — no copy duplicated in the scene.
- **AC6 — Gym-game parity.** `PlayScene` and every gym share `MineralChoiceScene`; no divergent render path or second overlay is introduced.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Scene tests cover: two-line wrapping of a long description, truncation/overflow safety, the one-line and no-description fallbacks, and non-overlapping row geometry.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** GDD §4.4.1 and the README entries for `MineralChoiceScene` / the hold-full overlay are updated from "one-line description" to a two-line description area; the docs guard (`src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts`) still passes.
- **AC9 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the change (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — description `wordWrap` width and `maxLines: 2`, plus dynamic vertical offsets / row pitch so a two-line description never collides with the detail line or the next option.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — wrap, truncation, fallback and layout tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4.1) and `README.md` — copy updates.
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — docs guard (extend if its wording assertion requires it).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which screen is "the hull full screen"?** Not asked interactively (downtime run with no producer present). Resolved by repository research: the phrase matches the hold-full choice overlay (the ship's hold, heading "HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP", `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`), the only full-screen surface that shows power-up/weapon descriptions without wrapping. Evidence: `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (description rendered at 13 px with no `wordWrap`), `src/scenes/HelpScene.ts` (gym help already wraps), GDD §4.4.1 "Hold full → power-up choice".
- **Q2 — Should the catalogue copy itself be lengthened to use both lines?** **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, producer):** this plan allocates a two-line area only and leaves the shared catalogue wording unchanged, preserving gym-help parity. If the producer prefers the copy itself to be extended, that is a follow-up item where the catalogue (`src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts`) and the gym help would change together.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 — plan skill (downtime run) after effort/risk pre-check `skip` (Extra Small / Low): appended goal, terminology clarification, current-behaviour evidence, documented assumption, 9 ACs, Key Files and the question Appendix; recorded the six review-stage notes and the AC coverage review in comments; effort/risk re-estimated (Extra Small / Low, ~1.1 h expected). No child work items created (single deliverable increment).

data.description:
# AI should focus fire on the boss

## Problem statement

The attract/demo AI pilot does not prioritise the Central AI boss. The boss is
exposed to the bot as an ordinary combat target (`contentId: 'boss'`), but the
shipped competent-bot content registry has no `boss` profile, so
`resolveEnemy('boss')` falls back to the neutral default (`threat: 1`). The bot
therefore weights the boss exactly like a scout and keeps shooting whatever is
nearest — typically minions and hazards — during the encounter, so demo runs
rarely read as a deliberate boss fight.

## Users

- **Audience of attract/demo mode** — a viewer watching the demo reach the boss
  wants the pilot to visibly attack the boss.
  - *As a viewer, I want the demo bot to focus its fire on the boss so the
    finale reads as an intentional boss fight rather than incidental
    minion-clearing.*
- **Game designers / balancers** — need a discoverable, single-source knob for
  boss prioritisation rather than a hard-coded constant.
  - *As a designer, I want the boss weighting expressed once in the bot content
    registry and its priority band expressed once in the tunables, so I can
    retune the behaviour without editing framework logic.*
- **Bot maintainers** — need the behaviour to follow the existing content,
  goal-band and parity conventions.
  - *As a bot maintainer, I want the boss rule to apply to both the final boss
    and the per-level mini-bosses through the existing `boss` snapshot target.*

## Existing state (evidence gathered)

- The production AI is the structured competent bot: `PlayScene` constructs
  `createCompetentBotBrain()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:571`). The legacy
  `decideBotIntent` path (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) is only a framework fallback
  adapter and is not used by `PlayScene` — it is **out of scope** here.
- `buildBotSnapshot` exposes the boss as `{ x, y, alive, phase }`
  (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:137`). `PlayScene.getBoss()` returns
  `this.miniBoss ?? this.boss` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200`), so **mini-bosses
  and the final boss both arrive at the bot as `contentId: 'boss'`**.
- `enemyTargets()` appends `{ x, y, contentId: 'boss' }` to the live enemy list
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts:180`).
- The enemy engagement goal scores `base + span × proximity × threat`
  (`weightedUtility`), and the engage behaviour selects a target with
  `bestWeightedTarget` — `threat / (1 + distance)` — both using
  `content.resolveEnemy(contentId).threat`
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts:224`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts:114`).
- `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT` registers every spawnable enemy archetype but **no
  `boss` profile** (`src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`), so the boss
  resolves to `DEFAULT_ENEMY_PROFILE` (`threat: 1`, `aim: 'direct'`, tunable
  engagement range of 140).
- Band arithmetic: `survivalBase 10`, `lifeBase 6`, `mineralBase 4`,
  `powerUpBase 3`, `enemyBase 2`, `asteroidBase 1`, `repositionBase 0.1`, with
  `prioritySpan 0.5`. A neutral-threat enemy band caps at **2.5**, so minerals
  and power-ups outrank combat today; a pure `threat: 2` boss reaches only
  **3.0** and still loses to minerals (4) and power-ups (3 + span).
- Target arithmetic: `weight / (1 + distance)` means a 2× boss beats a neutral
  enemy only while `1 + d_boss < 2 × (1 + d_enemy)` — roughly twice the
  competitor's distance. A minion at ~100 px still beats a boss at ~300 px (the
  usual boss standoff), so a content weight alone gives a **bias, not focus**.
- `BotBoss` exposes no `vx`/`vy`, so boss engagement aims at the current
  position rather than a lead (existing limitation; not changed here).

## Desired change

While a boss is alive and within the bot's enemy seek range, the bot makes the
boss its engagement target — regardless of nearer regular enemies — and keeps
firing at it instead of diverting to collection, with survival remaining the
only higher priority. The boss carries a weight of **2.0** (twice the neutral
enemy weight of `1`) in the content registry, and the boss-focus priority band
is expressed once in the competent-bot tunables.

Design sketch (the planner may refine details without changing intent):

1. **Content** — register a `boss` enemy profile
   (`{ id: 'boss', threat: 2, aim: 'direct', asteroidLike: false }`) in
   `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT`. Omitting `engagementRange` keeps the standoff
   single-sourced in `COMPETENT_BOT_TUNABLES`.
2. **Priority band** — add an `engage-boss` goal registered below `survive`
   (and `secure-life`) and above `collect-mineral`/`collect-powerup`, with a new
   `bossBase` tunable (e.g. 4.5, between `mineralBase` 4 and `lifeBase` 6). The
   goal is valid only while a live boss is inside the enemy seek range and is
   achieved/invalid when the boss dies or leaves range.
3. **Hard priority** — the `engage-boss` goal's target set is the boss alone, so
   the engage behaviour cannot pick a nearby minion. The boss stays in
   `enemyTargets()` (weighted 2.0) as the fallback when the boss band is invalid
   (e.g. out of range).
4. **Single source** — the weight lives in the content registry; the band base
   lives in `CompetentBotTunables` and is surfaced in the tuning fields and the
   bundled baseline like every other competent tunable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Boss profile and weight.** `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT.resolveEnemy('boss')`
   returns a shipped profile with `threat === 2` (twice the neutral `1`),
   `aim === 'direct'` and `asteroidLike === false`; a shipped-registry test
   asserts these values, and the unknown-content fallback is unchanged.
2. **Boss-focus goal band.** A dedicated boss-engagement goal is registered
   below `survive`/`secure-life` and above `collect-mineral`/`collect-powerup`,
   with `.base` sourced from the competent tunables; it is valid only while a
   live boss is within the enemy seek range and invalid once the boss dies or
   leaves that range.
3. **Hard priority and sustained focus.** With a live boss inside the enemy
   seek range and a **nearer regular enemy** also in range, the bot's committed
   goal is the boss goal, the engage target is the boss, and the boss stays
   committed across consecutive ticks (no flip-flop to minions).
4. **Survival first, collection subordinated.** A threatening incoming shot
   still selects `survive` over the boss goal, while milestones/power-ups never
   divert the bot while the boss goal is valid.
5. **Scope.** The behaviour covers both the final boss and per-level
   mini-bosses, since both surface as the same `boss` target in `BotSnapshot`;
   a snapshot-level test exercises the boss target and documents that mini-boss
   parity.
6. **Single-source tuning and guards.** The boss weight is read from the content
   registry (no duplicated magic number in goals/behaviours); the new band base
   is added to `CompetentBotTunables`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` (with a
   tooltip), and the bundled baseline configuration; the competent-bot docs
   guard test is updated deliberately for the new goal id.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` documents the boss profile in §11
   and the boss-focus band/priority order in §9 (including the `engage-boss` id);
   affected code comments are updated. CHANGELOG is excluded (release pipeline
   owns it).
8. **Validation gate.** The full project test suite passes with the new tests,
   run through `/skill:test` (repository test-execution policy); the new tests
   cover content, goals, behaviours and an integration scenario.

## Constraints

- **Content-first, core-light.** Prefer a content-registry entry for the weight;
  the new goal band is the minimum core change needed for hard priority and
  must follow the existing registry pattern (no `switch` on ids).
- **Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour lives in the shared competent brain, which
  the game and every bot gym consume — no divergent copy. `GymBotTuning` stubs
  `getBoss: () => null`, so it does not currently exercise boss engagement;
  adding a boss-capable bot gym is a non-blocking follow-up, not part of this
  change.
- **No gameplay changes.** Boss HP, phases, attack patterns, movement,
  mini-boss gating and boss VFX/audio are out of scope.
- **Read-only snapshot.** `BotSnapshot` stays read-only; no new mutation or
  scene coupling.
- **Tunables discipline.** Any new tunable must be added to
  `CompetentBotTunables`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` (with a tooltip) and the
  bundled baseline configuration, so the shipped tuning UI and docs stay in
  sync.
- **Legacy bot out of scope.** `src/ai/botDecision.ts` is not the production
  path; do not duplicate the rule there.
- **Scope creep.** General combat-over-pickups behaviour outside boss
  encounters, and boss aim-lead (needs `BotBoss` velocity), are separate work
  items rather than extra scope here.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` — Add the `boss` profile
  (`threat: 2`, `aim: 'direct'`, `asteroidLike: false`).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — Register the `engage-boss` goal, its
  validity/target set and the `COMPETENT_GOAL_IDS` entry.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — Handle the boss goal in the
  engage behaviour (boss-only target set / boss-first selection).

  documented default.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.test.ts` — Shipped boss profile and
  weight assertions.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — Boss-vs-minion
  priority, sustained focus, survival pre-emption and pickup subordination.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBotDocs.test.ts`,

  goal id / boss content.
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — Surface and baseline the
  new band base.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — Document the boss profile (§11) and the boss-focus
  band/priority order (§9).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200` — Evidence only
  (boss/mini-boss exposure); no change expected.

## Related work

- **Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids**
  (AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L) — established the band ordering this change refines
  with a boss band above collection.
- **Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour tree, predictive
  dodge/aim** (AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO) — the goals/behaviours and docs guards this
  change extends.
- **Content-adaptive configuration** (AH-0MUY08X98002TRHT) — the content
  registry and its documented extension path.
- **Enemy classification system for balanced wave design**
  (AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7) — origin of archetype threat/weight concepts.
- **Bot rotation skills** (AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98) — aim/lead handling reused by
  boss engagement.
- **Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core** (AH-0MUZMTS8J0029FSS) — the
  boss is a moving target; `BotBoss` still exposes no velocity.
- **Gym scene for AI bot tuning** (AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0) — stubs `getBoss: null`;
  boss-capable bot gym noted as a follow-up.
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry**
  (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) — the demo/attract context this improves.
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9 and §11; GDD §3.3 (mini-bosses) and §4.3
  (final boss).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "the AI" means the attract/demo pilot (the competent bot
  brain), not enemy AI.
- **Assumption:** "boss level" covers every boss encounter, because the bot sees
  mini-bosses and the final boss through the same `boss` target (producer
  decision 3).
- **Risk — minion pressure:** hard boss focus means the bot ignores minions
  that are not an imminent survival threat; minions may accumulate. Mitigated by
  the existing survival goal and predictive-steering hazard avoidance, and by
  the tuning band (`bossBase`) if playtesting shows it is too absolute.
- **Risk — demo pacing:** killing the boss faster changes showcase and capture
  timing; acceptable, but capture/showreel scenarios may need retiming.
- **Risk — moving-boss accuracy:** without `BotBoss` velocity the bot aims at
  the current position, so hits on a fast figure-of-8 phase may be fewer than a
  human's. Exposing boss velocity is a follow-up.
- **Risk — docs-guard churn:** adding a goal id breaks the competent-bot docs
  guard until `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` lists it; the guard update is deliberate.
- **Risk — baseline drift:** a new tunable must be added to the bundled baseline
  and tuning UI, or the demo will run with a value the producer cannot see/tune.
- **Scope-creep guard:** general combat-over-pickups behaviour outside boss
  encounters and boss aim-lead become linked work items.

## Resolved decisions (producer)

- **Q1 — Meaning of "2x":** **A** — twice the neutral enemy weight, i.e.
  `boss.threat = 2.0` (not 2× the tank, no multiplicative code path).
- **Q2 — Bias vs priority:** **B** — hard priority: while the boss is alive and
  inside the enemy seek range it is the engagement target regardless of nearer
  regular enemies; survival still outranks.
- **Q3 — Collection and scope:** **B** — a dedicated boss band below survival
  and above collection, applying to both the final boss and per-level
  mini-bosses.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — What does "2x" mean as a weight?** (Options: A 2.0 vs neutral,
  B 2.8 vs tank, C multiplicative factor.)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A — 2.0, twice the neutral enemy
  weight.** Final accepted answer. Source: producer reply to
  AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68 question comment; evidence: content registry contract in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` (neutral default `1`).
- **Q2 — Weighted bias or hard priority?** (Options: A 2× bias, B hard
  priority, C hybrid.)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): B — hard priority while the boss is
  alive and inside the enemy seek range, with survival higher.** Final accepted
  answer. Source: producer reply; evidence: `bestWeightedTarget` scoring in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` and band ordering in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`.
- **Q3 — Does focus fire outrank pickups, and does it include mini-bosses?**
  (Options: A enemy band only, B boss band above collection covering
  mini-bosses, C final boss only.)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): B — boss band below survival and
  above collection, including mini-bosses.** Final accepted answer. Source:
  producer reply; evidence: `PlayScene.getBoss()` returns `miniBoss ?? boss`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200`) and band bases in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` (`mineralBase 4`, `lifeBase 6`).

Research basis for the options: inspected
`src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`, `goals.ts`, `behaviours.ts`,
`tunables.ts`, `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` and `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200`;
searched the worklog for prior boss/bot-targeting items (no duplicate found).

# Stop firing when the boss is destroyed

**Headline:** Once the Central AI boss is destroyed the ship stops firing, so
the ship spawns no new bullets, muzzle flashes or shoot cues during the 5 s
in-run victory hold. The gate is a single shared hook in the combat core driven
by the per-run "run finished" state; in-flight bullets, the celebration and the
`GameOverScene` transition are unchanged.

## Problem statement

When the Central AI boss is destroyed, the run is over but `PlayScene` keeps
simulating the player for the whole `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS` (5 s) victory
hold before switching to `GameOverScene`. Because the shared player step still
runs auto-fire, the ship keeps shooting into an empty screen — bullets, muzzle
flashes and shoot cues continue underneath the celebration, which reads as the
ship still fighting after the fight is won.

## Users

- **Player who wins the run.** Wants the ending to feel like a victory, not
  like combat that quietly continues off-screen.
- **Demo / attract-mode viewer.** The recorded demo victory should show a
  finished ship during the fireworks, not one still firing.
- **Recording/capture author.** Wants the captured victory clip to show the
  celebration without stray player bullets and shot audio.

Example user stories:

- *As a player who has just destroyed the boss,* I want my ship to stop firing
  so the victory celebration is not cluttered by endless shots and shoot SFX.
- *As a viewer of a recorded victory clip,* I want the finale to read as "run
  over — celebration", not "still shooting at nothing".

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fire stops on boss destruction.** On the frame after the final boss
  phase is destroyed, the player's ship spawns no further player bullets, muzzle
  flashes or weapon fire cues for the rest of the in-run victory hold
  (`VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS`), up to the `GameOverScene` transition.
- **AC2 — Scope: run end only.** Suppression applies to the run-end (final
  boss) window only. Mini-boss defeats, wave/level transitions and the
  transition pause keep the current behaviour — the player remains in control
  and keeps firing (producer decision, Q1 option A).
- **AC3 — Shots already in flight are unaffected.** Bullets (and their
  lifetimes/collisions) that existed when the boss died keep flying and are not
  retroactively cleared or frozen; only *new* shots are suppressed.
- **AC4 — The shared beat clock does not freeze.** The beat clock drives the
  beat-modulated thruster hum (GDD §7.3) and player-fire scheduling; suppressing
  auto-fire must not stall it, so a test asserts the clock keeps advancing (or
  that the chosen gate provably cannot freeze it) through the hold.
- **AC5 — Gym↔game parity (documented divergence).** The suppression gate lives
  once in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) next to
  `autoFireEnabled()` / `isCaptureDisabled()` and defaults to "not suppressed".
  `GymBoss` is deliberately unchanged — it has no run-end, so it keeps firing
  after its boss dies — and that reason is documented in the code comment and
  the brief/GDD note, mirroring the `GameOverScene` precedent (GDD §7.2).
  Verified by the existing gym↔game equivalence suite plus a test asserting the
  shared hook's default is `false`.
- **AC6 — Re-run safety.** Starting a new run (scene restart) restores normal
  auto-fire — the suppression flag is per-run state, reset on scene
  create/restart, and a test asserts post-restart firing.
- **AC7 — Victory sequence unchanged.** The victory fanfare, juice and
  fireworks still trigger exactly once, and the delayed `GameOverScene`
  transition still happens at the end of the hold.
- **AC8 — Tests.** Automated scene-level tests cover the no-new-shots
  assertion for the whole hold, the in-flight-bullet behaviour, the clock
  continuity and the restart reset. `npm run typecheck`, the changed-scope test
  gate and (at push) the full suite pass.
- **AC9 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated: code comments
  on the new hook, GDD §2.3 (auto-fire) / §4.3 (boss) / §7.2 (victory
  celebration hold) noting that the ship stops firing once the boss dies, plus
  the gym-parity justification where relevant.

## Constraints

- No gameplay/balance change: score, lives, boss phases, celebration timing and
  the leaderboard flow are untouched.
- The gate belongs in the shared combat core (single implementation); no
  divergent copy in `PlayScene` or a gym.
- No new runtime dependencies; no new assets.
- The celebration must remain the dominant visual/audio signal — suppression is
  about removing noise, not adding effects.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageBoss()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:2870`) handles the lethal
  hit: it scores the final phase, calls `waveManager.onBossDefeated()`,
  `runTelemetry.bossDefeated()`, hides the boss health bar, calls
  `_triggerVictoryCelebration(x, y)` and then `_finishRunWithPurpose(true)`.
- `_finishRunWithPurpose(true)` defers `_finishRun(true)` by
  `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS` (`= ENDOFRUN_VICTORY_FIREWORKS_DURATION_MS`,
  5000 ms) so the in-run fireworks play; the scene keeps ticking during that
  hold.
- `PlayScene.tick()` runs `_tickPlayer(dt)` in every phase (including the
  wave/level transition pause) by design; `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer` gates
  auto-fire on `autoFireEnabled() && !isCaptureDisabled()` →
  `_autoFire(dt)` → `Player.tryFire(dt)` → per-weapon spawn + muzzle flash +
  `onWeaponFired` cue.
- There is **no** run-finished / victory gate today, so the ship fires for the
  whole 5 s hold. `GameState.defeatBoss()` exists but is *not* called from
  `_damageBoss()`, so `gameState.bossDefeated` is not a reliable signal.
- Precedents for gating player fire: `autoFireEnabled()` (opt-out per scene)
  and `isCaptureDisabled()` (temporary suppression during a tractor-beam
  capture), both in `CombatCoreScene`; the hold-full overlay instead drives a
  reduced-volume "ghost fire" from `MineralChoiceScene`
  (AH-0MV0QPO4N009KWVT).
- `GymBoss.damageBoss()` destroys its boss and stops there — the gym has no
  run-end screen and the player keeps auto-firing afterwards.

## Desired change

- Add one shared suppression hook in `CombatCoreScene` (e.g.
  `protected playerFireSuppressed(): boolean` returning `false`) and extend the
  `_tickPlayer` auto-fire gate with it, keeping the beat clock advancing while
  suppression is active (AC4).
- In `PlayScene`, record that the run is over when the boss dies (a per-run
  flag set before `_triggerVictoryCelebration`/`_finishRunWithPurpose`, reset on
  scene create/restart) and override the hook to report it.
- Leave already-spawned player bullets alone; do not clear enemy bullets,
  minions or hazards.
- Document the behaviour in the GDD and in code comments, plus the gym-parity
  statement per the Q3 answer.
- Tests in `PlayScene.test.ts` (hold-window suppression, in-flight bullets,
  celebration/transition unchanged, restart reset) and
  `CombatCoreScene.test.ts` (gate default + clock continuity).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — add the shared fire-suppression hook and
  wire it into the `_tickPlayer` auto-fire gate; keep the shared beat clock
  advancing.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — per-run "run finished" flag set in
  `_damageBoss()`; override the suppression hook; reset on create/restart.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts` — gate default, suppression and
  beat-clock continuity.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — existing gym↔game duplicate-body guard, run as the AC5 verification (no change expected).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — victory-hold no-new-shots test (reusing the
  existing boss-scenario boot helpers and `stepGameUntil`), in-flight bullets,
  celebration/transition regression, restart reset.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — **not changed** (Q3 option A): the gym has no
  run-end, so the shared hook's default keeps its ship firing; the divergence
  reason is recorded in the `CombatCoreScene` hook's code comment.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.3 (auto-fire), §4.3 (boss), §7.2
  (victory celebration hold) note the ship stops firing once the boss dies.

## Related work

- Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory (AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44) — *completed*;
  owns the 5 s in-run hold this item interacts with.
- Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice)
  (AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) — *completed*; the celebration the stray fire competes
  with; also the precedent for documenting a justified gym divergence.
- Wire PlayScene victory trigger (AH-0MUTYKKZ6001LT25) — *completed*; the
  `_damageBoss` → `_finishRun(true)` path.
- Hull Full overlay: metronomic fire sounds + restart countdown
  (AH-0MV0QPO4N009KWVT) — *completed*; the one existing case where player fire
  is deliberately decoupled from live gameplay.
- AI should focus fire on the boss (AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68) — *open*; adjacent
  fire-behaviour work, not overlapping.

Duplicate check: `wl search "boss destroyed firing"`, `"auto-fire victory"`,
`"player keeps firing"` and `"victory hold"` returned no item that already
satisfies these ACs.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Beat-clock freeze.* Suppressing `_autoFire` also stops the only per-frame
  `beatClock.advance()`, which the beat-modulated thruster hum reads. Mitigation:
  advance the clock while suppressed and assert continuity (AC4).
- *Ordering ambiguity on the lethal frame.* Boss destruction happens in the
  collision pass *after* `_tickPlayer` in the same tick, so one final shot may
  already be in flight. Mitigation: state the contract as "no new shots from the
  next tick" and test from the following tick.
- *Timing-sensitive existing tests.* The victory-hold transition test pumps the
  Phaser clock; changing tick behaviour could shift frame counts. Mitigation:
  keep the change additive and run the existing victory tests.
- *Scope creep* ("also stop enemy fire", "freeze the ship", "fade out SFX").
  Mitigation: keep to player auto-fire suppression; capture extras as linked
  work items.
- *Gym divergence.* A shared hook keeps the code single-sourced, but the gym
  behaviour question (Q3) must be answered rather than assumed — resolved as
  Q3 option A: shared hook default `false`, `GymBoss` unchanged, divergence
  documented.

**Assumptions** (confirmed by the producer in the Appendix)

- Suppression is triggered by the run ending, not by "no hostiles remain", so
  normal between-wave and mini-boss transition play is untouched (Q1 A).
- The ship keeps moving/thrusting during the hold; only firing stops.
- Existing player bullets are not cleared or frozen (Q2 A).
- `GymBoss` keeps firing after its boss dies; the absence of a gym run-end is
  the documented divergence (Q3 A).
- No change to the celebration duration, fireworks or transition timing.

**Sizing (recorded by the effort_and_risk step):** effort **Small**
(PERT O=2.25 h / M=4.50 h / P=9.00 h; expected 4.88 h, recommended 8.38 h with
overheads), risk **Low** (score 4/25, confidence 77%) — one shared hook, one
override, one per-run flag, tests and doc notes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of suppression.** Should the ship stop firing
  only during the final-boss victory hold, or also when a **mini-boss** is
  destroyed (each level's wave-10 mini-boss, after which the level transitions
  and the player keeps control)?
  - Options: **(A)** final boss / run-end only; **(B)** final boss **and**
    mini-boss defeats; **(C)** whenever no hostile remains on screen.
  - **Recommended: A** — it matches the request literally and avoids removing
    player agency during the mid-run mini-boss → level transition, where firing
    at leftover escorts/asteroids is still meaningful.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-25): A** — final boss / run
    end only. Recorded in AC2.

- **Q2 — Shots already in flight.** When the boss dies, should
  bullets already on screen keep flying (natural: they leave the screen within
  ~0.75 s), or be cleared/frozen for a clean celebration?
  - Options: **(A)** let them fly, suppress only new shots; **(B)** clear all
    player bullets on boss destruction; **(C)** freeze them (they stay on screen
    through the hold).
  - **Recommended: A** — least invasive, no visual "vanishing bullet" artefact,
    and no collision/cleanup special-casing.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-25): A** — in-flight bullets
    keep flying; only new shots are suppressed. Recorded in AC3.

- **Q3 — Gym parity.** `GymBoss` destroys its boss too but has
  no run-end screen. Should the boss gym's ship also stop firing once its boss
  dies (parity), or is "no run-end in gyms" the documented reason for
  divergence?
  - Options: **(A)** shared hook defaults to "not suppressed"; `GymBoss` keeps
    firing; the reason is documented (gyms have no run-end, mirroring the
    `GameOverScene` precedent in GDD §7.2); **(B)** `GymBoss` stops firing after
    its boss dies, exercising the same gate.
  - **Recommended: A** — keeps the gate single-sourced in the shared core while
    letting the gym keep exercising post-destruction behaviour; the divergence is
    documented rather than copied.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-25): A** — shared hook
    default `false`, `GymBoss` unchanged, divergence documented. Recorded in AC5.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCG5TUG006I7X1** – Destroy carried-over asteroids when entering the boss level (Phase 3) (completed)
- **AH-0MTHND272007XRBP** – GymEnemies: green Respawn button + Player on/off toggle (completed)
- **AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT** – If player crashes into an enemy, they both die (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: boss, destroyed, firing, players, ship (+2 more)
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — matched: boss, destroyed, firing, players, ship (+2 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: boss, destroyed, firing, players, ship (+2 more)
