# Bot should be aware of screen wrap around (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG)

## Problem statement

The game's playfield is a wrap-around (torus) arena — the player ship, asteroids,
bullets and raider patrol all cross a screen edge and reappear on the opposite
side — but the AI bot's decision layer (`src/ai/`) is wrap-blind: it treats the
four bounding edges as solid walls it must not approach, never crosses a seam on
purpose, and measures every distance, bearing, aim solution, threat prediction
and nearest-selection along the raw (unwrapped) straight line. A human player
routinely uses the seam to chase, flee and angle shots; the bot cannot, so demo
play looks unhuman, the bot camps near the walls it wrongly fears, and it
systematically misjudges everything on the far side of an edge.

## Users

- **Players / viewers of the attract demo** — the demo bot is deliberately
  human-like (human reaction cadence, W/A/D controls, thrust feel); humans use
  the wrap, so a bot that refuses to is conspicuous.
- **Developers** — one coherent torus model in the decision layer, so future
  features (seam-aware enemy fire, new archetypes, tuning) share a single
  implementation instead of adding seam hacks.

### Example user stories

- As a **player watching the demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge to
  reach a target that is closer the other way, so its movement looks like a
  human's.
- As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
  shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite
  edge — so engagements play out in the whole wrap-around arena.
- As a **player**, I want the bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
  across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming.
- As a **developer**, I want one wrap-aware geometry implementation used by
  steering, aim, prediction and distance, so the model is consistent and
  testable, and the headless eval measures the same physics the bot faces in
  the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wrap-aware steering (movement)** — The four arena edges stop being walls in
   the steering safety/clearance test: both the legacy `evaluateVector`
   (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) and the competent `evaluateDirection`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) no longer reject a direction
   solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`, and steering toward an
   objective uses the **shortest wrapped path** (the closer of the raw bearing
   and the seam-crossing bearing to the objective's opposite-edge duplicate) so
   the bot crosses an edge to get to the other side — used deliberately when
   net-positive (Q2), never as a scripted trick. Unit tests cover each of the
   four edges: the wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter; an
   edge-crossing direction is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.

2. **Seam-aware aim & targeting** — Aim and target selection run on the torus:
   `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the
   shortest wrapped path, and `nearestTarget` / `nearestEnemyDistance` choose
   nearest by wrapped distance. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or
   mineral is shorter than the raw line, the bot points at the seam duplicate —
   firing off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge. Tests assert the aim
   angle equals the wrapped-path angle when that route is shorter, and that
   behaviour is unchanged when the raw line is already shortest.

3. **Seam-aware threat & hazard prediction** — `predictIncomingFire`
   (`worldModel.ts`), the competent `closestApproach` solves and the legacy
   path-crossing checks operate on the wrapped torus, so shots and moving
   hazards whose closest approach to the player crosses a seam are predicted and
   dodged. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's existing wrap-jump clamp is
   re-verified so it does not double-compensate once positions are modelled on
   the torus. Tests: a seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening (a
   raw-line-only view would miss it).

4. **`wallMargin` retired cleanly** — The now-meaningless wall-margin tunable is
   retired (or demonstrably re-purposed) across `botDecision.ts`,
   `competent/tunables.ts`, `style/fitting.ts` and `tuningFields.ts`; saved
   bot-tuning configs (`src/data/bot-tuning.json` and any gym-saved tunings)
   still load with the field gone (unknown-field tolerance), and the style-fit
   mapping is updated per the retirement. Documented in the tuning UI/docs.

5. **Eval parity** — The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is brought
   to wrap-parity with the game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of
   being culled off-field, and hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped
   path (matching the seam-aware aim the enemy wrap epic ships), so eval scores
   measure wrap-aware play. `arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet and
   seam-aim cases.

6. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering
   (all four edges, raw vs. wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped
   nearest-selection when raw and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin
   retirement and eval parity. The human-like governor's reaction cadence,
   controls and thrust feel are unchanged (existing steering/bot integration
   tests stay green, plus new wrap scenarios). `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` are updated to describe the wrap-aware model. The full
   project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- One shared implementation in the bot decision layer — no divergent per-behaviour
  seam copies; share/adapt the seam maths the enemy wrap epic develops rather
  than reinventing.
- The human-like governor (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) is preserved: reaction
  cadence, W/A/D + optional reverse, seeded aim-skill noise and human-feel
  thrust presses are unchanged; wrap-awareness is a model property, not a
  scripted manœuvre.
- Use the seam when it is net-positive (Q2) — nearest-wrapped-path selection
  already yields that; no deliberate "wrap tricks".
- Do not change game physics (player/enemy/bullet wrap models); the bot's model
  must match the game, not alter it.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **Player wraps at all four edges** — `src/utils/movementModel.ts`
  (`if (x < 0) x += width; if (x >= width) x -= width;` and same for y). The
  headless eval arena drives the bot through the same `asteroidModel.tick(width,
  height)`, so the bot's own ship already wraps there.
- **Bullets wrap (game)** — `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` four-edge wrap;
  raider patrol wraps (`src/scenes/core/raiderPatrol.ts`). **Eval culls bullets
  off-field instead** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` `offField`), and hostile fire
  there aims at the raw player position.
- **Bot treats edges as walls** — legacy `botDecision.ts` `evaluateVector`
  ("a direction is unsafe when it reaches a wall within `wallMargin`") and
  competent `steering.ts` `evaluateDirection` (same); both tuned by a
  `wallMargin` knob (`botDecision.ts:189`, `competent/tunables.ts:239`,
  `style/fitting.ts`, `tuningFields.ts:94`).
- **All geometry is raw Euclidean** — `competent/goals.ts` `nearestTarget`
  (`Math.hypot`), `competent/steering.ts` `bearingTo` / `interceptPoint` /
  `closestApproach`, `worldModel.ts` `nearestEnemyDistance` /
  `predictIncomingFire`, `botDecision.ts` distance / closestApproach.
- **Existing wrap compensation, not awareness** — `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`
  deliberately clamps spurious position jumps caused by wrap/respawn.
- **Tests assert the bot never wraps** — `botSteering.integration.test.ts`
  ("it never wraps the screen").
- **Enemy wrap epic in flight** — AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 makes enemies wrap and fire
  across seams (blocked child slices AH-0MVKXBV0O005Q77P, AH-0MVKXBWDY008R0YH,
  AH-0MVKXBSAD003VRMF, AH-0MVKXBTNJ003F1TC, AH-0MVKXBXQX003S7K5,
  AH-0MVKXBZ5N007LKH4); once it lands, a wrap-blind bot fails to aim or dodge
  seam fire at all.

## Desired change

Give the bot's decision layer a single, shared wrap-aware (torus) model:

1. **Wrap-aware steering primitives** in the decision layer — a wrapped bearing /
   delta helper alongside the existing raw geometry, with a small hysteresis at
   nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths so targeting does not flip duplicates every
   tick; use it for the four steering/clearance tests (legacy + competent) and
   for `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint`.
2. **Wrapped nearest-selection** — `nearestTarget`, `nearestEnemyDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distances use wrapped distance; evade flees across a
   seam when that is the safest separation.
3. **Seam-aware prediction** — `predictIncomingFire` and the closest-approach
   solves run on the torus; verify `hazardVelocity` still clamps only true
   teleports.
4. **`wallMargin` retirement** — remove/re-purpose the knob and its style-fit
   mapping; keep saved configs loading.
5. **Eval parity** — wrap enemy bullets, aim hostile fire along the shortest
   wrapped path, and update `arena.test.ts` so metrics capture wrap-aware play.
6. **Docs & tests** — update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` / `docs/EVALUATION.md`; add
   the wrap-scenario tests from AC1–AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — wrap-aware `evaluateDirection`
  (no wall-margin wall test), `bearingTo`, `interceptPoint`, `closestApproach`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget` and goal distances on
  the wrapped torus.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `nearestEnemyDistance`, `predictIncomingFire`
  on the torus.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect/engage/evade distances
  and the evade flee direction.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — legacy `evaluateVector`, legacy aim/aim-delta and
  closest-approach paths.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts` — re-verify the wrap-jump clamp under the
  torus model; adjust only if double-compensating.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`,
  `src/ai/style/fitting.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`,
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — retire/re-purpose `wallMargin`; keep config
  loading tolerant.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` + `arena.test.ts` — wrapped enemy bullets, seam-aware
  hostile aim, parity tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` — describe the wrap-aware model.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`, plus a
  dedicated wrap-geometry unit test module.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** — "Enemies should be aware of the wrap around" (open
  epic with blocked child slices). Enemy counterpart: wrap-aware enemy movement
  and seam-aware enemy fire. Directly relevant — share the seam maths/helpers
  and sequence work so the bot and enemies land coherently.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed) — the wrap model the game's bullets use.
- **AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO** — "Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour
  tree, predictive dodge/aim" (completed) — the competent layer this change
  extends.
- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** — "Demo bot: human-like input limits" (completed) —
  the human-like governor whose look-and-feel must be preserved.
- **AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN** — "Predict enemy movement (bot)" (completed) — the
  hazard-velocity tracker whose wrap clamp interacts with the torus model.
- **AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV** — "Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay
  objects as the main game" (open) — bot/gym parity concern; watch for overlap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: duplicate flapping** — when the raw path and the wrapped path are
  nearly equal, a naive min-distance choice can flip between two seam
  duplicates every tick; mitigated with a small hysteresis/tolerance at near-equal
  lengths (the commitment layer already adds some hysteresis).
- **Risk: `wallMargin` migration ripple** — the knob appears across tunables,
  style-fitting, the tuning UI and saved `bot-tuning.json`; handle removal so
  saved configs keep loading, update the fit mapping, and document the behaviour
  change for old configs.
- **Risk: double-compensation** — `hazardVelocity` clamps wrap jumps today;
  once positions are modelled on the torus, verify the tracker only clamps true
  teleports/respawns and never swallows legitimate seam re-entry.
- **Risk: eval divergence** — the headless arena must mirror the game's wrap
  physics or wrap-aware behaviour earns no eval credit; keep the parity change
  minimal (bullet wrap + seam aim) and covered by `arena.test.ts`.
- **Scope-creep guard** — out of scope: game physics changes, non-torus
  pathfinding/routing, scripted wrap manœuvres, and any enemy/wrap changes
  beyond the arena-parity bump. Anything extra found becomes a linked work item,
  not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: dimensions** — the bot already receives playfield dimensions via
  tunables (`playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`, 960×540), so the torus needs no
  snapshot changes.
- **Assumption: seam maths reuse** — the enemy wrap epic (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8)
  will have developed wrapped-delta helpers; reuse/adapt rather than duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of wrap-awareness for the bot? (a) Movement/steering only. (b) +
  seam-aware aim/targeting. (c) Full torus model — plus seam-aware threat/hazard
  prediction." — Answer (Map): "(c) Full torus model". Source: producer reply on
  the work item (comment thread AH-C0MVR682R00022NOC). Research: steering walls
  in `botDecision.ts` + `steering.ts`, raw Euclidean geometry throughout
  (`goals.ts`, `worldModel.ts`, `behaviours.ts`), enemy wrap epic
  AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 in flight.
- Q2: "Should the bot deliberately *use* the seam as a manœuvre, or merely stop
  avoiding edges?" — Answer (Map): "Use it when net-positive". Source: producer
  reply on the work item. Research: nearest-wrapped-path selection yields
  net-positive seam use naturally; no scripted trick, human-like governor
  unchanged.
- Q3: "Should the headless eval arena be brought to wrap-parity with the game so
  eval measures wrap-aware play?" — Answer (Map): "Yes". Source: producer reply
  on the work item. Research: `arena.ts` culls enemy bullets off-field and aims
  hostile fire at the raw player position — both diverge from the game.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** – Enemies should be aware of the wrap around (open)
- **AH-0MU8FOQ7L005AII0** – Core Asteroid Entity + Unit Tests (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap

# Shard Swarm — fire/impact VFX & SFX

**discovered-from:AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW** (5 net-new weapon types) — audit of the `shard_swarm` player weapon found it shipped with an in-flight bullet look only: no fire sound, no muzzle flash and no per-weapon impact feedback.

## Current state (audit evidence)

Present:
- In-flight identity: `bulletShape: 'shard'` + overrides (`bulletShapeLength: 1.6`, `bulletTrail: 1.2`, `bulletSize: 0.72`, lime `BULLET_COLORS.shard_swarm = 0xc0ff33`) in `src/utils/weapons.ts:1336`, rendered through the shared bullet-shape seam (`_shard` in `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`).
- Code-drawn lime fan icon (`drawShardSwarmIcon`, `src/powerups/icons.ts:1121`).

Missing:
- **No fire SFX.** `playWeaponFireSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:628`) has no `shard_swarm` case, so it falls through to the `default:` no-op — the weapon fires silently in live play, in the hold-full metronome and in every gym.
- **No muzzle flash.** The definition declares no `muzzleFlash` metadata, and `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:896`) only spawns the launch cue `if (def.muzzleFlash)`.
- **No per-weapon impact feedback.** No `impactFx` spec, so `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` returns early: no baked hit cue (the impact is silent) and only the generic warm-white flash (`spawnBulletImpact`, `0xfff2a0`, r7, `CombatScene.ts:434`) rather than a lime shard-coloured one. The fan therefore reads as weak noise against the neon background at 0.72× bullet scale.

## Goal (user story)

As a player holding the Shard Swarm, I want an audible launch and hit so I can hear that the five-shard fan is firing and connecting, and I want the shards and their impacts to punch clearly against the neon field, so the weapon feels as distinctive in the hand as its silhouette suggests — without any change to its balance.

## Scope

`shard_swarm` only. Feel/visual/audio only — no behaviour or balance change: fire rate (750 ms, once per beat), the five offsets (±15°, ±7.5°, 0°), bullet lifetime (0.55 s → ~193 px reach), speed, size and colour stay exactly as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Audible fire.** `playWeaponFireSound('shard_swarm')` routes to a new baked ToneForge fire cue (recipe `aihell-shard-swarm-fire`, rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`), so live fire, the hold-full metronome and gym fire all sound identical through the one shared path (`src/audio/effects.ts`, `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`-adjacent registry pattern).
- **Audible, visibly distinct impact.** `shard_swarm` declares an `impactFx` spec (`color` = lime-family, `radius`, `duration`, `cue`) resolved through `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()`, producing a lime-tinted impact flash and a new baked hit cue (`aihell-shard-swarm-impact`) so the game and every gym connect identically. The generic white fallback flash no longer applies to this weapon.
- **Muzzle flash + more noticeable in-flight VFX.** The definition declares `muzzleFlash` metadata (lime, sized for a five-shard burst) spawned through the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path, and the shards are made more legible in flight (e.g. slightly stronger rim/spine contrast and/or a brighter trail) through the shared `bulletVisuals` seam — no per-scene copies, no new bespoke rendering path.
- **Gym↔game parity.** All changes land in the shared core/seams (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/`, `src/audio/`) and are consumed identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; `CombatScene.equivalence` and the gym-parity/documentation roster guards pass unchanged.
- **Docs + audio catalogue updated.** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` records both new cues with their recipes and seeds, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` lists them, and the per-weapon visual roster guards (`src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisualRoster.test.ts`) plus README/GDD §4.4/§7.3 per-weapon notes include the Shard Swarm's fire and impact identity instead of listing it as visual-only.
- **No new legibility regressions.** The five-shard fan at full upgrade levels (extra projectiles, larger bullets) must not become a screen-filling blur: the impact/muzzle flashes are rate-limited by the natural 750 ms cadence and the effect sizes stay within the existing per-weapon effect budget.
- **Full test suite passes**, including new/updated tests for the fire cue dispatch, `impactFx` resolution, muzzle-flash spawn, and the audio cue contract test (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`).

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `shard_swarm` `muzzleFlash` / `impactFx` metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — ensure the new metadata survives level resolution
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — in-flight `shard` legibility for the player weapon
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWeaponFireSound` case + impact cue registry + `playShardSwarm*Sound` exports
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-shard-swarm-{fire,impact}.yaml`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact seams (consume-only; no new hook needed if the metadata path suffices)
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README, GDD §4.4 / §7.3

## Known sibling gap (not in this item's scope)

The same missing feel package (`muzzleFlash`, `impactFx`, fire cue) applies to the other four net-new unlock-pool weapons from AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW: `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `heavy_slug`. Railgun SFX is already tracked by Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA); the remaining three have no item yet. The metadata/pipeline work here should be structured so those can reuse it unchanged.

## Risks / notes

- ToneForge assets are baked, not runtime-synthesised (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the sole runtime exception): new cues need recipe YAML + a `scripts/build-audio.sh` run, and the seeds must be recorded.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op in headless tests (no audio context).

# We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)

## Objective

**User story (producer).** As the producer, I want the region/home-world proposal
plus **two genuinely different** outer-loop candidates, each written up as a
decision-ready outline on the same footing, so that I can choose one and have it
written into the Game Design Document (GDD) with confidence.

**User story (player).** As a player, I want something to carry forward between
runs — a long-term goal and a sense that my play changes the world — so that
losing a run does not mean losing all progress, and so that beating the final
boss is a milestone on the way to winning rather than the end of everything.

## Users

- **Producer / designer (primary).** Chooses one of three outlined loops and owns
  the GDD write-up; needs comparable, honest outlines and a defensible ranking.
- **Player (arcade / bullet-hell fan).** Needs a reason to return after a lost
  run and a goal beyond a high score; wants progress that survives failure.
- **Developer / agent implementing the loop later.** Needs each outline to name
  the systems, seams and gym coverage so the chosen loop can be planned without
  re-deriving the design.

## Problem statement

The game has a strong **inner loop** (flying, dodging formations, destroying
enemies) and a functioning **middle loop** (per-run ship upgrading through
minerals → hold-full power-up choices → levelled weapons), but **no outer loop**:
nothing persists between runs except a leaderboard score, player settings and a
single run checkpoint. A death ends the run outright (GDD §4.6: "There is no
continue mechanic. Game over is final"), so long-term engagement rests entirely
on score chasing. The fiction ("pilot a resistance ship through a digital
underworld ruled by rogue AI") implies a war to be won, but the game currently
has no structure that represents winning it.

The producer has proposed one candidate outer loop (contested regions with a
home world to find and defend) and asked for **two other candidates** to be
brainstormed and outlined, after which the producer chooses one for the GDD.

## Deliverable

A single design-exploration document — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — built
to the same standard as the existing research catalogues
(`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`):
selected candidates written up per-concept, a "considered but not selected"
section, and a selection recommendation. It is a **design document only**: no
gameplay code, no persistence schema changes and no new scenes are implemented
in this item.

The producer's choice is then written into the GDD as a follow-on work item; this
item ends at the candidate document, the comparison and the recommendation.

## Loop tiers used by the document

| Tier | Timescale | Definition in this game | Exists today? |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------|
| **Inner** | Seconds | Flying, dodging, destroying enemies and formations within a wave | Yes (GDD §2.3–2.6) |
| **Middle** | Minutes (a run) | Ship upgrading: minerals → hold-full power-up/weapon choices, levelled effects, extra lives | Yes (GDD §4.4, §4.6) |
| **Outer** | Hours (a campaign / a season) | What the player carries **between** runs and what they are ultimately trying to achieve | **No** |

## Candidate A — Contested Regions / Home World (producer's proposal)

Recorded as proposed, not redesigned. Its outline must preserve every named
mechanic:

- Space is divided into **regions**; each region has an **AI aggression level**.
- The ship can **warp a limited distance** to adjacent regions.
- The goal is to find a region with **zero aggression** containing a **planet
  that can become home to the humans**.
- Having found it, the player must **defend all adjacent regions** against
  attack by aggressive AI.
- The player may leave their **fully upgraded ship** in a region with an **AI
  automated pilot** that defends that region.
- The player then returns home and **collects another ship with no upgrades**,
  and must go out again to make it strong enough to be left guarding another
  region.
- **Factional AI warfare** changes region strength over time: warring AI
  factions fight over a region and the winner leaves a stronger force there.
- **Win condition:** all regions have successfully defended against a massive AI
  onslaught, at which point the home world is safe and the game is won.

The outline must state its **minimal first slice** (the smallest version that
proves the loop is fun), because the full proposal is the largest of the three.

## Candidate B — Salvage Fleet (proposed direction, resource-persistent meta)

A **roguelite meta-progression** outer loop that leaves the map alone and
persists **player power** instead.

- Between runs the player spends **banked salvage** (minerals and mini-boss AI
  cores extracted at the existing checkpoint moments) in a persistent **hangar**
  to unlock hulls, starting weapons and permanent modifiers.
- Each run is a **deployment** flown in one chosen hull; losing the run forfeits
  that run's unbanked salvage but never the hangar.
- The outer goal is to assemble a fleet strong enough for a final assault run at
  maximum threat.
- Progression axis: **build/economy** (what the player owns), not territory.

## Candidate C — Signal Decode (proposed direction, knowledge-persistent meta)

A **campaign-mutating** outer loop where the thing that persists is
**information**.

- Mini-bosses and the boss drop **data fragments** that assemble a persistent
  codex revealing the origin of the AI and the "hellscape" it generates.
- Codex knowledge **mutates and unlocks the campaign** (new enemy behaviours,
  hellscape modifiers, shortcuts), and the final confrontation only becomes
  winnable once the core's rules have been decoded — the boss's phases are the
  codex's payoff.
- Progression axis: **knowledge and campaign variation**, not territory or
  currency.

## Required outline structure (every candidate)

1. **Fantasy / pitch** — one paragraph, in the game's fiction.
2. **Loop structure** — moment-to-moment → run → meta, with an explicit
   statement of *what carries between runs*.
3. **States** — win, lose, partial progress and what a bad run still advances.
4. **New systems** required (named, with rough size).
5. **Reuse of existing systems** — checkpoint (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`),
   minerals/power-up levels, `Leaderboard`, difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`), mini-boss rewards, bot/attract mode.
6. **Persistence and save model** — a sketch `localStorage` payload under
   §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend) with migration note.
7. **Session shape** — target run length and hours-to-win.
8. **UI / scene surface** — which new screens or menu entries are needed.
9. **Gym testability and the bot** — how its gameplay additions can be exercised
   in a gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule) and how attract mode can complete
   or avoid stalling on the outer loop.
10. **Pillar impact** — which current GDD pillars it changes (e.g. "no continue,
    game over is final", the single final boss), stated explicitly.
11. **Effort and risk** — sized honestly, with the failure modes that would make
    the loop unfun.
12. **Minimal first slice** — the smallest shippable version.

A **comparison table** then ranks all candidates on: fit with the existing
pilots-in-a-digital-hell fiction, reuse of shipped systems, new-system cost,
persistence complexity, session length fit, legibility of progress to the player,
gym/bot testability, and risk of trivialising or gutting the shipped campaign —
followed by an explicit **recommendation with rationale** and why the others rank
lower. A "Considered but not selected" section records further ideas (e.g. an
arcade-style tiered mutator ladder, a pure daily-seed challenge ladder) with a
one-line deferral reason each.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deliverable exists and frames the problem.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   exists, opens with the inner/middle/outer tier definitions above and the
   comparison criteria, and states that it is design-only.
2. **Candidate A is complete and faithful.** Candidate A is written up with all
   twelve required sections and preserves every mechanic listed in *Candidate A*
   above (regions, limited warp, per-region aggression, zero-aggression home
   region with a habitable planet, defence of adjacent regions, autonomous-pilot
   ship hand-off, unupgraded replacement ship, faction warfare, all-regions-held
   win). No proposed mechanic is silently dropped, altered or merged.
3. **Two additional candidates, materially distinct.** Candidates B and C each
   carry all twelve required sections and each names *what persists between
   runs* differently from Candidate A and from each other; each is justified
   against at least one named design pillar or fiction element.
4. **Decision-ready comparison.** The document contains a comparison table across
   the agreed criteria, an explicit recommendation with rationale, and a ranked
   justification for why the two non-recommended candidates rank lower.
5. **Alternatives recorded.** A "Considered but not selected" section lists at
   least two further outer-loop ideas with a one-line deferral reason each.
6. **Docs guard test.** A vitest docs-guard test (convention:
   `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`) asserts the document exists,
   contains the tier definitions, the comparison table and, for each of the three
   candidates, the twelve required section headings — so the deliverable cannot
   silently regress. It passes in the changed-scope test gate.
7. **Cross-linked, not orphaned.** The new document is cross-linked from the GDD
   future-scope section (§8) and from where the other design catalogues are
   referenced in `README.md`; every added link resolves to a file or anchor that
   exists.
8. **Producer decision is staged, not pre-empted.** The document ends with a
   "Producer decision record" section (candidate | decision | date | notes) left
   pending, plus a note that the chosen loop's GDD write-up is a follow-on work
   item. No GDD gameplay text for the chosen loop is written in this item.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `README.md`, and the GDD cross-links.
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Design only.** No gameplay, persistence-schema or scene implementation in
  this item; each candidate is marked "design only, not scheduled".
- **No backend.** All persistence must fit the existing `localStorage` model
  (GDD §6.6) with defensive parsing, as the leaderboard and checkpoint do.
- **Engine policy.** Candidates must not require a new engine or editor-driven
  content (GDD §6.1: code-first, Phaser).
- **Pillars are explicit, not accidental.** A candidate may propose changing an
  existing pillar (e.g. "no continue", the single final boss) but must say so in
  its *Pillar impact* section with a rationale and a cost.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any gameplay element a candidate proposes must be
  exercisable in a gym scene, and the outline must say how (AGENTS.md parity
  rule, `src/scenes/gym/`, `GymFormationScene`).
- **Attract mode must not stall.** The demo bot must be able to traverse or skip
  any new outer-loop UI (§2.1 attract/demo mode).
- **Scope discipline.** Opportunities discovered mid-draft become linked work
  items, not added scope.
- **Write location and language.** Deliverable lives in `docs/` (no planning
  documents in the repo root); UK English and Markdown throughout.
- **Session shape must be stated.** Each candidate names its target run length
  and its hours-to-win, so the producer can compare commitment.

## Existing state

- **Inner/middle loops shipped:** 10-level campaign, 100 waves, 10 mini-bosses,
  one multi-phase final boss (GDD §3, §4.6); minerals and hold-full power-up
  choices are the middle loop's currency (§4.4); difficulty scaling is data-driven
  (`src/core/levelScaling.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`).
- **Persistence today:** `ai_hell_leaderboard` (top-10 scores), `ai_hell_settings`,
  `ai_hell_checkpoint` (auto-written at each mini-boss defeat and offering
  "Continue — Level N"), `ai_hell_lastSession` (GDD §6.6).
- **No meta layer:** no persistent currency, unlock tree, map/region structure or
  cross-run progression of any kind. Game over is final (GDD §4.6).
- **Design-document precedent:** `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` and
  `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` are the established pattern for
  candidate-selection research, each with a sibling docs-guard test
  (`src/classicEnemyResearchDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`).

## Desired change

The repo gains one decision-ready design document describing three outer-loop
candidates on equal footing, with a comparison, a recommendation, deferral
reasons for rejected ideas and a docs guard that keeps the document honest — so
the producer can choose one loop with full information and the GDD write-up can
start immediately afterwards.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — **new**; the deliverable (candidate outlines,
  comparison, recommendation, deferrals, producer decision record).
- `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` — **new**; docs guard asserting the
  document's required sections and per-candidate headings, following the
  `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts` convention.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **edit**; §8 Future Scope cross-link to the new
  document (no gameplay text for a candidate in this item).
- `README.md` — **edit**; add the new document where the other design catalogues
  are referenced.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — **reference only**; the existing between-level
  persistence seam any outer loop will build on.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` —
  **reference only**, to ground each candidate's reuse claims.

## Out of scope

- Implementing any candidate's systems (map, currency, codex, hangar, regions).
- Writing the chosen loop into the GDD as playable specification (follow-on item).
- Balancing or tuning anything that already ships.
- CHANGELOG.md (managed by the release pipeline).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — deliverable shape.** "Brainstorm two other possible outer loops
  and write an outline for each" is read as a design-exploration deliverable in
  `docs/`, matching the existing research-catalogue precedent, with Candidate A
  (the producer's proposal) included so the two alternatives are compared fairly.
- **Assumption — no implementation.** "I will choose one to be written up in the
  GDD" means the GDD write-up is the *next* item, so this item stops at the
  decision-ready document.
- **Risk — pillar conflict.** Every attractive outer loop tends to break "game
  over is final" or the single-final-boss structure; mitigated by the mandatory
  *Pillar impact* section and by stating each candidate's cost explicitly.
- **Risk — Candidate A is very large** (region graph, autonomous pilots, faction
  simulation). Mitigated by requiring a *Minimal first slice* per candidate.
- **Risk — scope creep into implementation** while drafting. Mitigated by the
  design-only constraint and by filing discovered opportunities as linked work
  items.
- **Risk — over-specified docs guard.** The guard asserts headings and required
  terms only, never prose wording, so the document stays editable.
- **Risk — comparison feels arbitrary.** Mitigated by publishing the criteria in
  the document before the candidates (AC1) and ranking against each.

## Related work

- **Game Design Document for AI_Hell (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — the living GDD this
  document feeds; §2.3–2.6 (inner loop), §4.4/§4.6 (middle loop, level
  progression), §5–§6 (leaderboard, save data), §8 (future scope).
- **Checkpoint save/resume (AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51)** — the existing persistence
  precedent the outer loop extends or replaces.
- **New enemies from classic arcade games (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52)** and
  **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4)** —
  the candidate-selection research pattern this document follows.
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry
  (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4)** — the bot that must remain able to traverse any new
  outer-loop UI without stalling.
- **Update campaign documentation for 10-level structure (AH-0MV39AQOY006I083)** —
  the campaign-structure documentation the outer loop will eventually supersede
  as the game's framing.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience
  (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775)** — the validation lens the recommendation must survive.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No interactive interview round was run in this pass: the item was auto-dispatched

# In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget

Discovered during **AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES** (verify fix with full suite and a
manual long-run soak), discovered-from **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE**.

## Observation

A 5-clip full-run soak (`--count 5 --max-duration 1800000 --diagnostics`,
output written to `/tmp/ah-soak/`) completed every clip, but the process node
RSS peaked at **661.0 MiB** (clip 4 start) — above the documented **< 512 MiB**
target. The peak is not recording growth: it is `peakRssBytes` at the *start*
of a clip, carried over from the **previous** clip's end-of-clip probe, and
every clip's end-of-recording RSS was 320–388 MiB.

Cause: clips 3 (34.9 MiB) and 5 (62.75 MiB) are above the 32 MiB in-page probe
threshold, but their files sat outside the served repository root
(`/tmp/ah-soak/…`), so the probe fell back to the **in-page Blob** path
(documented fallback, reported by `probeSourceReason`). That fallback decodes
up to the 32 MiB retained prefix with `decodeAudioData` in one shot, which
inflates node RSS by a few hundred MiB temporarily. A control run of the same
workload with the output inside the repo root (`capture-output/soak/`,
600 s, 48.43 MiB) used the **streamed** probe and peaked at only **408.9 MiB**.

## Why it matters

The < 512 MiB budget is documented for a full-cap run, and `--output /tmp/…`
is a supported, documented invocation. The *path*-based fallback (and its RSS
cost) is not covered by the parent's stated fallback rationale, which only
sanctions the in-page decode for clips *below* a size threshold.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Document, in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` §Long-run memory budget, that
   the streamed probe needs the output inside the served repository root and
   that the in-page fallback costs a temporary whole-prefix audio decode
   (with the measured 661 MiB batch peak vs 408.9 MiB streamed as the
   evidence), or
2. Make the streamed probe work for outputs outside the served root (e.g. a
   temporary route serving the partial file), restoring the < 512 MiB budget
   for every supported output path.
3. Re-run a > 32 MiB clip with `--output /tmp/…` and record the peak RSS
   against the budget.

## Evidence

Full numbers, per-clip diagnostics and logs: comment on
AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES; diagnostics artefacts under `/tmp/ah-soak/`
(`batch-1..5.diagnostics.json`) and
`capture-output/soak/soak-streamed2.diagnostics.json`.
data.title: In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget for long clips written outside the served repo root

# Force Field bubble: permanent persistence + spent-dim

Parent: AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14 (More forcefield feedback). Producer decisions: Q1 = **b (dim when spent)**, Q2 = **c (bounce flash + new baked cue)**, Q3 = **feature** — see the parent's Appendix.

## Goal (user story)

As a player who has earned the permanent Force Field (hold-full reward), I want the bubble to stay visible for the whole run, and to **dim** — not vanish — when its reflect budget is spent, so I can tell "field up" and "field up but spent" apart, and never confuse either with the temporary-pickup countdown.

## Problem (confirmed root cause)

`drawForceFieldBubble` (`src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts:304`) gates the draw on `registry.remaining('force_field')` — the **temporary-window** countdown. A permanent-only field is stored with `remaining: 0` (`_startOrRefreshTimed`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`), and a permanent base whose temp window expired is reset to `remaining = 0` (`_expireTimedEffect`). So the bubble is drawn for at most the temp window (base 8 s) and then cleared even though `isForceFieldActive()` stays true for the rest of the run.

## Implementation sketch

1. Keep the existing `isForceFieldActive()` check first (it already is), then replace the gate with the temporary-window semantics the HUD already uses (`powerUpTemporaryRemaining('force_field')`, `src/powerups/effects.ts:1512`):
   - draw when `powerUpTemporaryRemaining('force_field') === undefined` (permanent base, no temp window → permanent-only), or
   - draw when the returned window countdown is `> 0`;
   - otherwise (window countdown `0`, or inactive) clear and return `false`.
   - `powerUpTemporaryRemaining` returns `undefined` for **both** "permanent-only" and "effect absent", so the `isForceFieldActive()` guard must stay ahead of it.
2. Add exported spent-state constants — `FORCE_FIELD_SPENT_STROKE_ALPHA` and `FORCE_FIELD_SPENT_FILL_ALPHA` — distinctly fainter than `FORCE_FIELD_STROKE_ALPHA` (0.9) / `FORCE_FIELD_FILL_ALPHA` (0.14) yet still visible, each documented with a comment citing AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14 Q1 = b ("up but inert", never "expired").
3. When `registry.forceFieldRemaining() <= 0`, use the spent alphas as the **baseline** for stroke and fill (rim pulse preserved, scaled down). The existing final-second ending brighten applies **on top of the baseline** and only for an active temporary window (`tempRemaining !== undefined`); a permanent-only or spent-permanent bubble has no ending brighten.
4. Pulse phase: for a temporary window keep using its countdown (unchanged); a permanent-only field has no countdown, so a steady (constant-phase) rim pulse is acceptable — document the choice in a comment and keep the diff minimal.
5. Update the `forceFieldAt` test helper in `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` to expose `powerUpTemporaryRemaining` (undefined = permanent-only, number = temp window) **and** `forceFieldRemaining`. Re-express the existing "clears and draws nothing at expiry (remaining 0)" test with a temp-window fake returning `0` so it keeps its meaning (a temp-only field at expiry), and keep "clears when inactive" as-is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Permanent bubble persists:** with a permanent (hold-full) Force Field and no temporary window, `drawForceFieldBubble` returns true (draws) while `isForceFieldActive()` is true, every frame, for the whole run — including after any prior temp window on top of it has expired. Unit test with a permanent-only fake registry in `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`.
- **AC2 — Spent field dims, never vanishes:** while the field is active but the reflect budget is exhausted (`forceFieldRemaining() <= 0`), the bubble is drawn with the reduced spent-state alphas (new exported constants pinned by test), for permanent and temporary fields alike; the bubble is **not** cleared by budget exhaustion. A spent permanent bubble sits steady (no ending brighten); a spent temporary bubble still runs its final-second ending brighten relative to the dim baseline.
- **AC3 — Temporary window behaviour unchanged:** with an active temporary window (with or without a permanent base underneath) and positive reflect budget, the bubble is drawn with the existing final-second brighten.
- **AC4 — Expiry still clears:** inactive field → graphics cleared, `drawForceFieldBubble` returns false (existing tests stay green).
- Spent constants are exported, `> 0`, and strictly less than the corresponding active alphas (pinned by test).
- The draw gate no longer derives permanence from `registry.remaining('force_field')`; tests exercise the permanence path through `powerUpTemporaryRemaining` so a regression to the old gate fails a test.
- Only the bubble module and its test change: the three scene call sites compile untouched.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — gate, `FORCE_FIELD_SPENT_*` constants, comments.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` — `forceFieldAt` helper + new/updated tests.
- Verify-only call sites (no edits expected): `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (~3736), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (~1218), `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` (~468).

## Constraints

- Shared core only — no scene-local copies (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- Reflect-budget semantics unchanged; budget regeneration is out of scope (AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P).
- Surgical diff: do not refactor the enemy force-field bubble that lives in the same module.
- TDD: write the failing test first, then the minimal code, and commit only green (repo commit gate).
- No docs beyond code comments here — the GDD row is in the docs/verification sibling.
data.title: Force Field bubble: permanent persistence + spent-dim

# Intercept feedback: bounce flash + dedicated baked reflect cue

Parent: AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14 (More forcefield feedback). Producer decision Q2 = **c**: the intercept feedback is a bounce-point flash **plus a new baked ToneForge cue** (one new asset is explicitly authorised; `audio/toneforge/pin.json` must not change).

## Goal (user story)

As a player, every bullet my Force Field reflects should flash at the bounce point and make its own dedicated "bounce" sound, so I can tell a reflection from a bullet destruction, a ricochet tick, or taking a hit — and so game and gyms read it identically.

## Context

**Reflect seam (shared core):** the reflect path is one shared loop in `CombatScene` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:1289-1304`): an enemy bullet overlapping the bubble where `effects.tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` succeeds calls `_reflectEnemyBullet(eb)`. `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts:3264` pins `_reflectEnemyBullet` as shared, so feedback added in this branch reaches `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene` with no scene edits.

**Flash precedent to reuse** (no new VFX helper): `spawnBulletImpact(scene, x, y, { registry, color })` (`src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`) — a self-destroying flash tracked in `this.bulletImpactEffects`, already used at `CombatScene.ts:1511` (`_spawnEnemyBulletHitImpact`) and by the enemy-field absorb seam (AH-0MVM8GW7W004SI0E AC3).

**Baked-cue pipeline** (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J): every baked cue needs a data-only recipe in `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-*.yaml`, a manifest entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (cue → recipe, delivery `baked`, reserved seeds), a deterministic render (`node scripts/build-audio.mjs --render`) into `public/audio/sfx/<recipe>.<seed>.wav`, and a checksum pin in `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`. `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` derives the typed view straight from the manifest (no second edit). The contract suite (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) asserts every sound-producing export is manifest-mapped.

Seed check (verified during planning): the manifest's highest reserved seed is **32275** (`aihell-arc-impact`), so **32276** is the next free seed.

## Implementation sketch

1. **Recipe** `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-forcefield-reflect.yaml` — a short bright "bounce", deliberately distinct from `aihell-bullet-destruction` (square tick 1400→900 Hz) and `aihell-ricochet-impact` (soft high bounce tick 1800→900 Hz). Header comment records the amplitude target: **subtle one-shot, target RMS 0.055 ±1.5 dB**.
2. **Manifest** entry: `{ cue: "playForceFieldReflectSound", recipe: "aihell-forcefield-reflect", delivery: "baked", seeds: [32276] }`, next to the other baked one-shots.
3. **Export** in `src/audio/effects.ts`: `export function playForceFieldReflectSound(): void { playCue('playForceFieldReflectSound'); }` with JSDoc recording the decision (baked fresh per Q2 = c, **not** an alias like `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound`, which reuses `playBulletDestructionSound`).
4. **Render + pin:** `node scripts/build-audio.mjs --render`, then commit `public/audio/sfx/aihell-forcefield-reflect.32276.wav` together with the updated `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`. `audio/toneforge/pin.json` unchanged.
5. **Balance-guard classification** (decided during planning): `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` identifies **enemy** cues by recipe tag (`ENEMY_TAGS` includes `bullet`). Recommended: tag the recipe `player`, `force-field`, `reflect` (no enemy tag) so the cue sits outside the enemy balance guard, with the 0.055 subtle-one-shot target documented in the recipe header and `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`. Adding `playForceFieldReflectSound: { targetRms: 0.055 }` to `AMPLITUDE_TIERS` (which additionally subjects the cue to the guard's A-minor pitch and peak-ceiling checks) is permitted provided the guard stays green. Record the route taken in a work-item comment.
6. **Wire the seam** in the shared reflect branch (prefer the branch over `_reflectEnemyBullet` so the latter stays a pure bullet factory and the equivalence duplicate-body guard stays trivially green): on each successful reflect,
   - `spawnBulletImpact(this, bulletX, bulletY, { registry: this.bulletImpactEffects, color: FORCE_FIELD_COLOR })` at the enemy bullet's current position (before its graphics are destroyed);
   - `playForceFieldReflectSound();`
   - exactly one flash and one cue per intercepted bullet.
7. **Docs row:** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — new cue row (cue, recipe, description, seed 32276) plus the tier line if a tier was registered.
8. **Tests** in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` (harness already exposes `bulletImpactEffects`): reflect one bullet → exactly one flash registered, coloured `FORCE_FIELD_COLOR` (0x33ffcc) at the intercept position, and the cue spy called once; reflect two bullets → two flashes / two cue calls; no reflection (field inactive or budget spent) → no flash and no cue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC5 — Intercept flash:** every bullet the field reflects spawns one short-lived flash at the intercept point, registered in the shared `bulletImpactEffects` registry (observable in tests), coloured `FORCE_FIELD_COLOR` (0x33ffcc).
- **AC6 — Intercept SFX (new baked cue):** every reflected bullet plays `playForceFieldReflectSound()`; the cue has a manifest entry (recipe `aihell-forcefield-reflect`, delivery `baked`, seed 32276), a rendered WAV committed under `public/audio/sfx/`, an updated `checksums.json`, and a callable export in `src/audio/effects.ts` with the decision documented. The audio contract suite (cue coverage) and the amplitude-balance guard stay green.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity:** flash and cue fire from the shared `CombatScene` reflect branch, so `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene` get them with no scene edits; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard stays green; no new divergent copies.
- Each intercepted bullet produces exactly one flash and exactly one cue call; a non-reflected enemy bullet (field inactive or reflect budget exhausted) produces neither.
- The flash is spawned at the enemy bullet's intercept position (asserted), not at the player centre.
- The recipe renders deterministically (double `--render` reproduces the pinned checksum), `audio/toneforge/pin.json` is unmodified, and the new seed 32276 is unique in the manifest.
- `playForceFieldReflectSound` is not an alias: its manifest `recipe` differs from every other cue's recipe.
- The cue-mapping doc gains the new row with recipe, seed 32276 and amplitude tier, and the balance-guard route chosen is recorded.
- No scene file is edited by this item (`git diff --stat` touches only shared core, its test, `src/audio/`, `audio/toneforge/`, `public/audio/sfx/` and the cue-mapping doc).

## Key Files

- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-forcefield-reflect.yaml` — **new** data-only recipe.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new baked-cue entry (seed 32276).
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-forcefield-reflect.32276.wav` + `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — rendered asset (never hand-edit the WAV).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` (+ `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) — export + cue decision comment; contract coverage.
- `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` (+ test) — only if the tier route is chosen.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — reflect branch feedback call site (flash + cue).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — flash + cue seam tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — verify-only (duplicate-body guard stays green).
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — reused flash (no change expected).
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — cue row / tier line.

## Constraints

- Shared core only; **no** scene-local flash or cue (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- No new VFX module, no explosion particle burst (bullets are ~3 px), no second new audio asset.
- Data-only recipe: no ToneForge engine code changes; do not re-render or re-seed any existing cue.
- TDD: write the seam test and the contract expectation first, then the implementation; commit only green (repo commit gate).
- UK English in docs and comments; CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

As a maintainer, I want the Force Field bubble/spent-dim behaviour and the new reflect cue documented in the design and audio references, and the whole repository suite proven green, so the change is auditable and safe to release.

## Scope

1. **GDD power-up row** — `docs/Game Design Document.md` line ~880, `force_field` row: state that the bubble persists while the field is active (including the permanent hold-full field), that it **dims** when the reflect budget is spent (never vanishes), and that each reflected bullet flashes at the bounce point with a dedicated cue (`playForceFieldReflectSound`). UK English, consistent table style.
2. **Audio reference** — `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`: confirm the cue row/seed/tier added by the intercept-feedback sibling is complete and consistent (fix gaps if any; do not duplicate the row).
3. **Code comments audit** — read the diffs of `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` and `src/audio/effects.ts`: each touched seam carries a comment explaining the behaviour and citing AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14, and the spent-dim rationale (Q1 = b) is discoverable from the constants.
4. **README / parity docs** — check whether `README.md` or `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention) needs a line; add only if genuinely missing (no invented scope).
5. **Full-suite verification** — run the repository test workflow through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`), never ad-hoc test commands, and triage any failure into a critical `test-failure` item per the triage policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC10 — Docs:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — at minimum the `force_field` row in `docs/Game Design Document.md` (permanent bubble persists and dims when spent; reflected bullets flash at the bounce point with a dedicated cue), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (new cue row + seed + amplitude tier), and code comments in the touched modules (CHANGELOG.md excluded — owned by the ship pipeline).
- **AC9 — Testing/validation:** the implementation is validated by the repo's test workflow; AC1–AC8 regression tests pass.
- **AC11 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
- **AC8 — Test coverage:** at least one unit test per changed seam exists and is green — bubble persistence (AC1), spent-dim rendering (AC2), the reflect-feedback seam (flash + cue once per intercept), the manifest/cue-coverage contract, and the shared constants (verified by reading the diffs and the suite result).
- The verification is performed *after* both implementation slices land; failures are either fixed here (trivial) or filed as blocking critical `test-failure` items (never silently waived).

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — `force_field` power-up row (~line 880).
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — cue catalogue consistency.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — parity convention (verify-only unless a line is missing).
- `README.md` — verify-only unless a line is genuinely missing.
- Verify-only: `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`, `src/audio/effects.ts` comments.

## Constraints

- Documentation only plus the suite gate — no behaviour changes here; if a behaviour fix is needed, raise it as a child of this parent and note it.
- Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md` (ship pipeline owns it), `.pi/`, `skill/` or other agent infrastructure.
- Test runs go through the test skill; no ad-hoc `pytest`/`npm test`/`vitest` invocations.

# Orbital Strike does nothing

## Problem statement

The **Orbital Strike** power-up is functionally wired but reads to the player as
doing nothing: it produces **no sound at all** and reuses the generic Smart Bomb
AOE ring instead of an orbital bolt, so nothing about it says "an orbital strike
just happened". Worse, in the two most common situations the bolt is **silently
consumed with zero feedback** — no VFX, no SFX, no damage.

## Users

As a **player**, I want picking up an Orbital Strike to produce an unmistakable
event — a bolt falling from the sky onto the target with its own sound — so that
I can tell the power-up is working, and so that the permanent (hold-full) reward
is worth the choice.

As a **player**, I do not want a pickup wasted silently when it is collected
while no enemy is alive; I want the strike to land on the next target (or be
clearly signalled as unused).

## Existing state (repo research)

The power-up is **not** dead code — the damage path exists and is tested. What is
missing is the *feedback layer* plus two silent-failure paths.

1. **State + decision (working).** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` sets
   `_strikePulsePending = true` for a field pickup and `_strikePermanent = true`
   + a pulse timer for a hold-full reward (`src/powerups/effects.ts:644`).
   `EffectsRegistry.updateStrike(dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts:1241`) returns
   `true` exactly once for a queued pickup and then once per
   `strikeInterval()` (`max(10, 30 − 2×level)` s) for the permanent reward.
2. **Shared detection (working).** `CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike`
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1655`) is called from `_tickPlayer`
   (`:878`) and forwards to the `onOrbitalStrike(damage)` hook, so the game and
   every gym run one implementation.
3. **Application (working, but visually generic).**
   `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:642`) picks the
   live enemy nearest the ship, then spawns
   `spawnNovaRing(..., ORBITAL_STRIKE_RADIUS = 40, ORBITAL_STRIKE_COLOR = 0x9ffcff)`
   plus `spawnBulletImpact(...)` and applies `damageEnemyViaAoe(target, damage)`.
   That is **the same nova-ring helper and colour family as the Smart Bomb
   pulse** (`onSmartBombPulse`, `CombatScene.ts:673`) — there is no descending
   bolt, no target marker, no telegraph, no screen flash/shake. The ring lasts
   `NOVA_RING_DURATION = 0.5` s (`src/vfx/aoeEffect.ts:25`), so it is easy to miss
   entirely during play.
4. **No SFX exists.** `src/audio/effects.ts` exports **no** orbital-strike cue
   and `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (66 cues) has **no** strike entry. The
   `onOrbitalStrike` body makes no `play*` call. The unrelated Missile-Command
   **hazard** entity (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) borrows
   `playScoutAdvanceCue` (`docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md:94`), which is
   why the hazard is audible and the power-up is silent.
5. **Silent-waste path A — no target.** `onOrbitalStrike` returns early when no
   live enemy is found (`CombatScene.ts:646`), but `updateStrike` has **already**
   cleared `_strikePulsePending`. A pickup collected between waves is therefore
   consumed with literally no effect: "it does nothing at all".
6. **Silent-waste path B — no player.** `_updateOrbitalStrike` does not guard on
   a live player; `onOrbitalStrike` does. Same silent consumption.
7. **Weak readout.** The HUD shows a `strike` row **only** while the strike is
   permanent (`src/ui/HUD.ts:523`) and never shows the time to the next bolt, so
   even an armed permanent strike looks inert.
8. **Damage is often invisible.** `strikeDamage()` is `1` hit at level 1
   (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:979`), so a bolt on a multi-HP enemy removes
   one pip and on a 1-HP grunt is indistinguishable from an ordinary bullet kill.

## Desired change

Give Orbital Strike a distinct, legible identity and remove the silent failures:

- A **descending orbital bolt** (beam/column from off-screen top down to the
  target) ending in a bright impact flash — its own VFX module, not the Smart
  Bomb ring.
- A **new dedicated SFX cue** (`aihell-orbital-strike`, baked WAV), played at the
  bolt's impact.
- **No silent consumption**: a queued bolt with no live target (or no live
  player) is **retained** and fired on the first valid frame rather than being
  discarded.
- The HUD `strike` row shows the countdown to the next bolt for a permanent
  strike.

> Scope confirmed by the producer (2026-10-28): this work item covers the
> **power-up** only; the Missile-Command `orbital-strike` hazard is out of scope
> except for non-regression (AC7).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Distinct visual identity.** A strike (field pickup or permanent pulse)
   renders a descending bolt from the top of the play area onto the target plus
   an impact flash, through a new VFX module in `src/vfx/`, and the visual is
   demonstrably distinct from the Smart Bomb pulse (different shape/composition,
   not just a recoloured `spawnNovaRing`), asserted by unit tests on the module.
2. **Dedicated audio cue.** A new `playOrbitalStrikeSound` cue exists in
   `src/audio/effects.ts`, backed by a **new** ToneForge recipe
   (`aihell-orbital-strike`, baked WAV built via `scripts/build-audio.sh`),
   registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, and played by the shared strike
   path; `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` and `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`
   stay green.
3. **No silent waste.** A strike that resolves while no live enemy (or no live
   player) is present is **not** lost: the queued bolt is **retained** and lands
   on the first frame with a valid target. A regression test drives a pickup with
   no live enemy and asserts the bolt subsequently lands on the next live enemy.
   At most one bolt is retained (a permanent strike simply resumes its interval)
   so a long enemy-free gap cannot bank a volley.
4. **Damage path unchanged.** The bolt still applies `strikeDamage()` hits to the
   nearest live enemy through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, and still depletes enemy force
   fields through the shared `takeDamage()` seam —
   `src/scenes/core/enemyForceFieldDamageSources.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` stay green.
5. **Gym↔game parity.** The VFX/SFX and the no-silent-waste behaviour live once
   in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and are consumed by `PlayScene` and
   every gym; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (duplicate-body
   guard) and a gym parity test in `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`
   stay green, and the strike is observable in the gym.
6. **HUD countdown.** A permanent strike's HUD row shows a live countdown
   (`next in Ns`) to the next bolt, asserted by a HUD test.
7. **Hazard reviewed, not regressed.** The unrelated Missile-Command
   `orbital-strike` hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) is confirmed
   unaffected by this change; its suite (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.test.ts`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` §"Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike")
   stays green.
8. **Testing/validation.** Every acceptance criterion above is covered by an
   automated test that fails before the change and passes after it.
9. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — including code comments, the GDD §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section
   (following the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" precedent, which documents
   the aura and cue beside the mechanics), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
   for the new cue, and any relevant README or wiki entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory.** No divergent copy: shared behaviour in
  `src/scenes/core/` (and shared dispatchers), consumed by `PlayScene` and every
  gym scene. Any intentional divergence must be recorded in this work item and in
  a code comment.
- **Audio goes through the cue pipeline.** A cue may not be synthesised ad hoc:
  it needs a `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` entry plus a recipe under
  `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, and (for `baked` delivery) a rebuilt WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`. The contract suite asserts every `play*` export is
  manifested.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- Cosmetic/feel work only — do **not** re-tune strike damage, interval or drop
  weight as part of this change unless a tuning defect is found (record it as
  linked follow-up work instead).
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onOrbitalStrike`: replace the generic
  `spawnNovaRing` composition with the new bolt VFX and the new cue.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateOrbitalStrike`: retain/requeue a
  bolt when no target or no player is available (the no-silent-waste seam).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `updateStrike`: expose a requeue/retain path so a
  decided bolt is not lost.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts` — **New.** Descending bolt + impact-flash VFX,
  registered like `src/vfx/thornsAbsorb.ts` / `aoeEffect.ts`.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.test.ts` — **New.** VFX composition/distinctness tests.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — **New** `playOrbitalStrikeSound` wrapper.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `audio/toneforge/recipes/` — **New** cue
  entry (`aihell-orbital-strike`) and recipe.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — document the new cue row.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — `next in Ns` countdown on the permanent `strike` row (AC6).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section: strike
  visibility + cue paragraph.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — gym parity + observability test.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (now confirmed):** "Orbital Strike" in the report means the
  **power-up** (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.strike`, display name exactly "Orbital
  Strike"), not the Missile-Command `orbital-strike` **hazard**. Confirmed by the
  producer (Q1 → (a)); the hazard is out of scope except for non-regression
  (AC7). Rationale: the hazard already has a telegraph, a falling shell, a
  detonation burst and a borrowed cue, whereas the power-up has no cue at all.
- **Risk — new audio asset cost.** A new dedicated recipe plus a WAV rebuild is
  required (Q2 → new strike SFX). This is the largest single risk: the ToneForge
  recipe must be authored, baked and manifested, and the baked asset must survive
  the audio balance guard. Budgeted as its own WBS item.
- **Risk — VFX legibility vs. visual noise.** A full-height bolt on every pulse
  may fight other screen effects; cap its draw to the target column and keep the
  duration short, and validate in `GymPowerUpsCombat` with a live player.
- **Risk — retarget semantics.** Retaining a queued bolt could stack up several
  bolts during a long enemy-free gap. AC3 caps the retained queue at one bolt (a
  permanent strike simply resumes its interval) so the behaviour stays
  predictable and testable.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Levelling, drop-weight and interval tuning, a strike
  "charging" telegraph, and multi-target strikes are all tempting; they are
  **out of scope** and should be captured as linked follow-up work items rather
  than absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** the "[no] VFX" complaint refers to the *generic, unnoticeable*
  ring rather than a rendering defect — no rendering bug was found in research.

## Related work

- **Some power-ups appear to do nothing (AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z)** — wired this
  power-up's gameplay consumers (commit `154b7adb`); AC5 covered damage only, not
  VFX/SFX.
- **Orbital Strike substrate (AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — catalogue, level curves,
  effects-registry accessors and HUD readouts for the net-new power-ups.
- **Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike (AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1)** — the
  unrelated enemy hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`); reviewed for
  non-regression only.
- **Orbital-Strike falling shell projectile identity (AH-0MV822GIO005B685)** —
  the hazard projectile's visual identity; a useful precedent for giving the
  power-up its own identity.
- **Create E4 Phaser gym scene (AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13)** / Phaser orbital work —
  unrelated (`orbital` formation kind, not this power-up).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 (power-up levels, Orbital Strike row) and
  the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" paragraph in the same section — the
  documentation precedent for describing a power-up's VFX/SFX.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — the cue catalogue the new sound must
  join.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — gym↔game parity convention.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which "Orbital Strike" does this report mean: the power-up or the
  campaign hazard?**
  Options: (a) the **power-up** (`strike`, "Orbital Strike" pickup/choice
  reward); (b) the Missile-Command **hazard** (`orbital-strike` enemy entity);
  (c) both.
  **Recommended:** (a) the power-up — it has literally no SFX and only a
  borrowed generic AOE ring, which matches "no VFX or SFX".
  — **Answer (producer): (a) the power-up** — the `strike` power-up
  ("Orbital Strike"). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-28. The Missile-Command
  `orbital-strike` **hazard** is therefore **out of scope**, reviewed for
  non-regression only (AC7). Research evidence supporting the answer: the
  power-up has zero audio cues and a generic 0.5 s ring; the hazard has a
  telegraph, a falling shell, a detonation burst and the borrowed
  `playScoutAdvanceCue`.

- **Q2 — May we add a new baked SFX cue, or must we reuse an existing one?**
  Options: (a) **new dedicated recipe** (`aihell-orbital-strike`) + baked WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`; (b) **reuse an existing electric recipe** (e.g.
  `aihell-arc-fire`) with no new asset; (c) no new audio, make the visual carry
  the identity.
  **Recommended:** (a) a new dedicated recipe — an orbital strike is a signature
  event and should not share a cue with the arc weapon.
  — **Answer (producer): a new dedicated strike SFX cue** — option (a). Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-10-28. Binding constraint: the cue needs a new ToneForge
  recipe (proposed slug `aihell-orbital-strike`) plus a baked WAV built via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`; `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`,
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and the audio contract tests
  (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`) must be
  updated in the same change.

- **Q3 — Should the permanent strike's HUD row show a countdown to the next
  bolt?**
  Options: (a) yes, add `next in Ns`; (b) no, keep the row as-is.
  **Recommended:** (a) yes — a 10–30 s interval is otherwise invisible, and the
  HUD already renders countdowns for other timed effects.
  — **Answer (producer): (a) yes** — add a `next in Ns` countdown to the
  permanent strike's HUD row. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-28. AC6 is now a
  required criterion rather than an optional one.

- **Q4 — Is it acceptable that the strike retains a queued bolt when no enemy is
  alive (rather than being wasted)?**
  **Recommended:** yes — silently losing a rare pickup is the reported bug.
  — **Answer (producer): yes, retain the bolt** — a queued bolt is retained and
  lands on the first frame with a valid target. Source: interactive reply,
  2026-10-28. AC3 is now the retention behaviour (retarget), not the alternative
  "signal as unused" path.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1** – Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike (completed)
- **AH-0MV5DFBVW002J2XO** – Orbital Fires in direction of orb (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: anything, don, fact, nothing, orbital (+5 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: doing, don, fact, nothing, orbital (+4 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: don, fact, nothing, orbital, sfx (+3 more)

> Automated report only; the curated **Related work** list above is authoritative.

# Setup seam: weapon levels and forced mineral reward

Dev-gated extension of the shared scene-`setup` seam (parent AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB, parent AC2 parts (a) and (c), plus AC4 for seed/level determinism). Makes weapon levels 2-5 and the Hull Full pay-off expressible in a capture config **without** any shipped-game behaviour change.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can write `"player": { "weaponLevels": { "rapid": 4 } }` in a scene config and get a scene that starts with a level-4 rapid, and I can force the full-hold resolution to the Hull Full reward so the pay-off lands on camera deterministically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — `player.weaponLevels` is a first-class setup field.** Validated and normalised in the pure `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` module (per-weapon integer levels within the documented range 1-5 for capture use), typed in `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts`, and accepted on every setup-capable target that already consumes `setup.player` (or documented as restricted, if restricted). Unknown weapon ids raise the existing `unknown-weapon-id` code; invalid levels raise a documented code.
- **AC2 — The applier implements weapon levels through the existing seam.** `applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) grants `weaponLevels[id] = N` as N permanent `equipWeapon(id, true)` calls, and `SceneSetupState` gains the typed field. `player.weapons` keeps its level-1 semantics unchanged. A scene without the field is byte-for-byte behaviour-compatible with today.
- **AC3 — `setup.mineralReward` forces the hold-full resolution.** `SceneSetupState` and the parser carry an optional reward id; `GymLevel._resolveMineralHold` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`) resolves to that reward when configured (through the shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`) and falls back to today's `randomChoiceStrategy` when absent. An unknown/unavailable reward id is rejected at parse time rather than silently ignored.
- **AC4 — Dev-gating holds.** `npm run check-bundle` stays green (no new production surface) and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stays green (the change configures existing state through the shared applier; no divergent gameplay copy).
- **AC5 — Tests from F1 turn green.** The relevant assertions in `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` and `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` pass; failures are fixed in code, not by relaxing the tests (any genuine spec change is recorded as a comment on both items).
- **AC6 — Error codes are documented in the module.** Each new code is added to `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES` with a doc comment, and is listed in `SCENE_SETUP_COMMON_FIELDS`/target-extra-fields as appropriate so the docs parity test can see it.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — validation/normalisation/error codes/field lists.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` — `SceneSetupPlayer.weaponLevels`, `SceneSetup.mineralReward` declarations.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — `SceneSetupState` + `applySceneSetup` weapon-level grants + reward selection seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — `_resolveMineralHold` honouring the forced reward.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` — tests from F1.

## Dependencies

Blocked by F1 (test-first contracts).


## Plan traceability

- **Parent AC2 — deterministic arc beats via a small dev-gated setup extension.** The scene `setup` seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` to gyms) gains, with validated and normalised support in `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` plus `.d.mts` types and error codes: `player.weaponLevels` (per-weapon permanent levels 2-5), `setup.bossHitsRemaining` (the boss gyms `GymBoss` and `GymMiniBoss` spawn their entity with that many hits left) and `setup.mineralReward` (the hold-full choice in the level gyms resolves to that reward id). Each new field is validated, normalised and documented alongside the existing ones; the extension is dev-gated and inert for production, `npm run check-bundle` and the gym-game parity suite stay green, and no shipped-game gameplay behaviour changes.
